#28584. Grand Theft Auto 6 Review: a Once in a Generation Open-World Achievement

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1663 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

Grand Theft Auto 6 Review: a Once in a Generation Open-World Achievement

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If there’s one thing Rockstar can never be accused of, it’s rushing out Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s not like Rockstar wasn’t busy during that time — they’ve been constantly updating the ever-growing Grand Theft Auto Online and also happened to release one of the greatest westerns of all time in Red Dead Redemption II.
  • It has been revealed that GTA 6 centers around the complicated personal and professional relationship of two criminals, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and their journey through the realistically hard-to-succeed-in world of Vice City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there’s one thing Rockstar can never be accused of, it’s rushing out Grand Theft Auto VI. It’s been so long since the (still incredible) GTA V debuted that there are people who weren’t born at the time who are now teenagers (no, you’re not old enough to play yet, son, and go to bed!).

Recent findings suggest that it’s not like Rockstar wasn’t busy during that time — they’ve been constantly updating the ever-growing Grand Theft Auto Online and also happened to release one of the greatest westerns of all time in Red Dead Redemption II. Yet all of the many years of development somehow becomes immediately apparent the second you pass the title screen. Put simply, this is one of the largest and most ambitious games ever created.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 centers around the complicated personal and professional relationship of two criminals, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and their journey through the realistically hard-to-succeed-in world of Vice City. That’s about the only story element I’m comfortable sharing, however, as this is a game that begs not to be spoiled and to be experienced as fresh as possible.

GTA VI’s main story is full of crazy twists and turns, surprising emotional beats, and yes, absolutely hilarious moments that push boundaries and envelopes. Along the way, you’ll meet a cast of colorful characters that will rapidly endear themselves to you and ones you’d commit many virtual felonies to defeat out of seething hatred.

While the campaign is gripping and exciting all the way through, there are so many stories just waiting to be discovered in GTA VI. It feels like a living, breathing world which is all the more impressive considering there are basically no loading times or slow down upon entering a loaded save.

Industry observers note that there’s a ton of traffic through the roads (so much so that you can’t just easily blaze through like a bowling ball as easily as in previous games), the drivers get actively mad if you crash into them, and there are NPCs going about their days on every corner. You could make a whole game into simply approaching NPCs and seeing what they’re up to — there are some surprisingly interesting happenings going on and it’s rare that even the most minor of characters repeats themselves.

According to recent reports, while you can follow the main story all the way through, complete tons of side quests or simply take part in what the most depraved of us do and make the game into a rampage simulator, there are so many activities here that almost any one of them could be focused on as a full game. There’s diving for treasure, bird watching, fishing, customizing cars and oh so many other things that are fully fleshed out and not just throwaway afterthoughts.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, just existing in the game is so complex now that GTA has basically become a life sim. Upon awakening, you can eat, make coffee, watch TV, play video games, workout, watch a show, do home repairs, feed pets and enough other tasks to make a list of them as long as a full review.

It’s incredibly cool for the world to feel so realistic that you literally sometimes get stressed out from knowing you have to do a chore and can’t just go run people down (I guess I am one of the depraved ones after all). Sometimes an hour is spent in GTA VI literally lifting weights, drinking a protein drink, grocery shopping and laying down in bed doomscrolling. While that might not exactly be the sentence to sell you on the game, the fact that GTA VI is just that deep and manages to make it all enjoyable to carry out truly speaks to the attention to detail at play.

Recent findings suggest that the realism also carries over into the gameplay mechanics themselves. Driving feels more realistic than it ever has. It’s easy to get wanted stars and hard to shake the cops, and people will get actively pissed off at you for doing the wrong thing. In fact, it’s realistic to the point that some might not have as much fun as they did in previous titles as you will think twice before hijacking a random car or even parking it in the wrong place (yes, the fuzz can be called on you for leaving your car at an NPC’s house).

Just existing in the game is so complex now that GTA has basically become a life sim.

It goes beyond simply just blazing through the world doing horrible things and hoping a cop doesn’t see it — there are immediate and severe consequences to your actions now.

That being said, it’s hard to criticize Rockstar for the game being too realistic, and once you adapt to its ebb and flow, this new realistic GTA experience feels all the more enveloping as it stimulates the anxiety, stress and fear synapses as much as the happiness ones, making successful accomplishments in the game all the more rewarding.

Sources indicate that it’s impossible to review GTA VI without touching on the music, and if I had my way, this entire review would just be speaking about that. But as I don’t want to risk you clicking out since we could really use those GTA page views, I’ll keep it short.

Sources indicate that the score itself is composed by famed French electronic duo, Justice, and is like an aural hug to the ears. The instrumentals during key action scenes are some of the best heard since HEALTH’s stunning Max Payne 3 score and get the adrenaline pumping.

The included original songs Justice recorded are so expertly crafted to sound like ‘80s hits that I was literally googling the lyrics thinking I had found long lost ‘80s songs before realizing it was actually Justice. Considering I’m significant Justice fan who’ve seen their live show multiple times, that states a lot that they even fooled me.

Industry observers note that it’d be fair to judge a GTA by its radio stations as they play such an integral part in the experience and are heard for literally hundreds of hours by most players, so thankfully there’s another incredible lineup here. There’s a channel for everybody — ranging from buttrock to country to reggae to classical music to many, many more.

In a recent development, fans of past channels like Radio Broker and Radio Mirror Park will be happy to hear that there’s another hipster/indie style channel in GTA VI dubbed “Stockyard FM” which plays music from the likes of Hot Chip, Nation of Language, !!! and even debuts a newly introduced song from the aforementioned HEALTH. Flash FM rapidly becomes a favorite as well, focusing on high energy dance pop and electro pop from artists like Billie Eilish, The Ting Tings and more.

It has been revealed that finally, Circoloco Records is a commendable addition featuring smooth throwback-style electronic music from Rockstar’s own record label. But expect to hear a fantastically curated soundtrack no matter which station you jam out to, with artists ranging anywhere from The Weeknd to Steve Winwood.

It has been revealed that with how many flawlessly-executed mechanics and elements to GTA 6 there is, it’s hard to find faults. There’s not even many glitches that occur, which is shocking for an open world game of the magnitude.

In a recent development, possibly the only criticism would be that it's so complex and ambitious that the learning curve is steep, and even after dozens of hours in the game, it’s easy to forget how a certain mechanic works or which button does what at times. Of course, criticizing something for being so deep proves difficult and at the very least perhaps a good problem to have in the end.

Rockstar has minimized the complexity as much as they could by providing an easy-to-access control list at all times and basically devoting the first twenty or so hours of the story as a backdoor tutorial.

Considering how enormous the scope of GTA 6 is, it’d be easy to forgive it for having visuals not up to snuff, yet it boasts some of the most realistic character models seen in gaming and uses them throughout all of the beautifully-choreographed in-game cutscenes.

Sources indicate that the way the characters are rendered give them a certain unique realistic element that has never quite been captured before — from unique body types to random skin marks to life behind the eyes. As good as the characters look, the environments might look even better with everything from trees to the pavement itself rich in detail. There’s also incredible lighting work at play that makes everything pop like you’d expect Florida, er, Vice City to.

According to recent reports, while it may seem impossible for anything in our universe to live up to the hype and anticipation Grand Theft Auto 6 has garnered, Rockstar has done the impossible. GTA VI offers more in a single package than any video game before it, blowing past its status as one of the best action games of all time into one of the best life-sims of all time. And one of the best driving games of all time. And one of the best…birding…games of all time? It may sound like hyperbole, but GTA VI is so chock full of content that it feels like several fully-fleshed out games in one. And that’s not to mention it actually does have several fully-fleshed out games within a game inside of it. GTA VI may not completely reinvent the wheel, but it fully commands it, delivering an enormous adventure that’s chock-full of enough things to keep you busy until Grand Theft Auto VII (please, Rockstar?). The last thirteen years were more than worth the wait and make Grand Theft Auto VI go down as an unparalleled achievement in video games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar has finally proven the doubters wrong, as Grand Theft Auto VI is officially tied for the best-reviewed video game of all time, with only Nintendo’s greatest retro title managing to keep up.

Expectations for Grand Theft Auto VI were sky-high going in, especially after being delayed on multiple occasions, with Take-Two and Rockstar promising that the game needed more polish and would be worth it in the end. There were some doubters, but the fact that Take-Two was leaving money on the table meant that most fans had faith it would live up to expectations.

Sources indicate that the embargo for Grand Theft Auto VI went up as soon as the game went live on Latest Zealand’s Microsoft Store, and the scores are in. It seems that Rockstar is ending 2026 with a bang, as Grand Theft Auto VI has obliterated the competition, at least in terms of reviewer opinion.

The Metacritic page for Grand Theft Auto VI is live, and the results are in. Grand Theft Auto VI’s MetaScore is 99, making it tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, with a huge range of 10/10s from outlets worldwide.

One outlet that gave Grand Theft Auto VI a 10/10 is DualShockers, with Steve Hennley writing, “While it may seem impossible for anything in our universe to live up to the hype and anticipation Grand Theft Auto 6 has garnered, Rockstar has done the impossible. GTA VI offers more in a single package than any video game before it, blowing past its status as one of the best action games of all time into one of the best life-sims of all time.”.

Grand Theft Auto VI’s MetaScore is 99, making it tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, with a huge range of 10/10s from outlets worldwide.

In a recent development, the only game to match Grand Theft Auto VI’s MetaScore is the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64, which also has a 99. Funnily enough, the game’s remake came out this year, and it scores slightly lower than Grand Theft Auto VI, capping out at a 96 on Metacritic.

That being noted, a trip to Hyrule might be the only option for a lot of people, as Grand Theft Auto VI is currently a PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S exclusive. This means that Nintendo Switch 2 and PC owners will have to find out games to play. Maybe it’s time to break out Garfield Kart and pretend he’s running over civilians?

It was always likely that Grand Theft Auto VI would score well, considering Rockstar’s amazing library of titles and the sheer amount of time and money that went into its latest game. The delays might have been frustrating, but if the result was the best-reviewed game of all time, then it was worth it.

The question now is what the fans will think, as only people in Fresh Zealand can presently play the game. Oh, and the people on Xbox Series X/S who have suddenly traveled to Middle-earth and switched their region to New Zealand (don’t worry, no one will tell John Microsoft). After all, it’s not unheard of for the critical and audience reviews to differ greatly.

The verdict from the fans will filter in over the next few days and weeks, but until then, Rockstar and Take-Two can lean back and know they have a stacked accolades trailer ahead of them, and that Vice City will have millions of visitors over the upcoming holiday season. If the reviewers are correct, a once-in-a-generation game has arrived, and it’s time to dive in.

What All Floppy Disks Do In Dice Hoarder

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that one of the main features of Dice Hoarder is that skills level up through the floppy disks you can find throughout the shop.
  • According to recent reports, however, when you pick them up, it helps to know what each one does.
  • As you make your way through the shop and start clearing up some of the dice, you'll find floppy disks lying around in places you might've just looked and not seen anything.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that one of the main features of Dice Hoarder is that skills level up through the floppy disks you can find throughout the shop. It adds a bit of mystery once you start getting emails about their enigmatic appearance and what they could mean, but that doesn't make them any less useful.

According to recent reports, however, when you pick them up, it helps to know what each one does. Some are self-explanatory, while others might not be clear from the name alone. Regardless, they make your job significantly easier, especially once you level them up. Here are all the floppy disk abilities in Dice Hoarder and how to use them.

As you make your way through the shop and start clearing up some of the dice, you'll find floppy disks lying around in places you might've just looked and not seen anything. When you pick them up, you can identify them only by their color and title.

According to recent reports, however, when you install them on the computer, you'll find two types of disks: magical and non-magical. The non-magical ones affect your personal abilities or have some... messages on them, while the magical ones make sorting through the dice a breeze.

The non-magical abilities are some of the most useful because they function as quality-of-life updates to your overall character.

Lets you sprint, with consecutive upgrades increasing sprint speed.

Lets you crouch to get lower to the floor and see under tables.

Lets you pick up dice from farther away, with consecutive upgrades increasing that distance.

Lets you place dice into slots from farther away, with consecutive upgrades increasing that distance.

While these are the only non-magical floppy disks that affect your stocking, some floppy disks don't give you abilities but provide story context in the campaign.

You'll have to play through the campaign to properly understand the context of those disks, but as you can imagine, it's not quite as pleasant as the rest of the game.

The magical abilities are what really make stocking the shelves faster and easier. These are the things you couldn't do yourself if you were stocking the shelves of a die shop in real life.

Highlights and draws a line to the correct display for the held die so you don't have to check the computer every time.

Creates a ring around you in which any dice for your held set are highlighted to make them easier to find.

In a recent development, summons dice from your held set to you from wherever they are in the store. Upgrading it more will summon more dice at a time.

While you're holding a d20, activating this will roll that die, and upon a passed check will complete the set and automatically fill the slot on the display.

These abilities are the best way to organize every die in the store as fast as possible, but be warned. If you want all the achievements, you have to complete the game without using any of these. You can still use the non-magical floppy disks, but the magical ones void the final achievement in the game.

The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences (AIAS) has unveiled that Shigeru Miyamoto, the creator of iconic Nintendo franchises like Super Mario and The Legend of Zelda, will receive the inaugural Legend Award at the upcoming 30th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards ceremony on Thursday, 18th February 2027.

The award, which will only be presented once per decade, 'recognises an industry icon whose enduring vision continues to redefine interactive entertainment'. It's designed to honour creators whose achievements have already earning lasting universal acclaim, while celebrating their 'immeasurable impact and influence'.

Meggan Scavio, President of the AIAS, noted the following:.

“Shigeru Miyamoto is widely recognized as one of the most respected and impactful figures in the games industry and beyond. We believe he perfectly embodies our inaugural Legend Award through his impact and reach, and we are so humbled and excited to have Mr. Miyamoto accept this award at the 30th anniversary of the D.I.C.E. Awards.".

Though his current focus is on the production of movies and theme parks, Miyamoto-san is arguably the most recognisable figure in Nintendo's history, and it's difficult to imagine whether the organization would even exist today without his creations.

Recent findings suggest that he most recently appeared during a Pikmin Day Direct presentation, during which he revealed a new demo for Pikmin 4 on Switch 2 along with some Pikmin Bloom updates and the commencement of monthly Hello! Pikmin movies on the Nintendo Today app.

#28577. Ashes of the Singularity 2 review: Some neat ideas undermined by a rubbish campaign and obtrusive generative AI

Ashes of the Singularity 2 review: Some neat ideas undermined by a rubbish campaign and obtrusive generative AI

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1845 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ashes of the Singularity 2 has some neat ideas for army management, but a poor campaign, an underwhelming new faction, and obtrusive generative AI use undermines the enterprise.
  • In a recent development, PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you.
  • Industry observers note that what is it?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ashes of the Singularity 2 has some neat ideas for army management, but a poor campaign, an underwhelming new faction, and obtrusive generative AI use undermines the enterprise.

In a recent development, PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

Industry observers note that what is it? RTS sequel in the lineage of Supreme Commander.

Reviewed On: AMD Ryzen 5 3600, Nvidia 2080 Super, 32 GB RAM, Windows 10.

Ashes of the Singularity 2 can't be faulted for scale. Much like its predecessor, the RTS sequel delivers on the promise of letting players control truly colossal armies. Rolling up huge globs of units and tossing them at your enemy lines in a giant, explosion-riddled mud fight is never subtle and only occasionally clever. But for any veteran RTS player, watching miles-long lines of armies clash is inevitably going to stir the soul.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, scale is also the sum of what Ashes of the Singularity 2 offers. As a sequel, it does little to build on the strengths of the original, while largely failing to address that first game's weaknesses. The campaign is terrible, the story borderline incomprehensible, and the whole experience is overshadowed by the spectre of generative AI.

In a recent development, before we get into Ashes 2's numerous problems, I do want to give Oxide Games credit for one thing: for a game of this scale, Ashes of the Singularity 2 is remarkably easy to control. In terms of base-building, Ashes of the Singularity 2 is a largely familiar RTS affair. You build your production buildings, your resource harvesters, your defensive structures, and that's more or less it.

It has been revealed that when it comes to unit recruitment, however, Ashes 2 is much more interesting. While units are still recruited individually, they're also automatically assigned into armies at the recruitment phase. You build a upcoming army by queueing up all the units you want, and then when you're done, you assign a rally point for the army on the map, and all the units will just assemble there.

According to recent reports, once recruited, armies can be selected with the number keys and controlled like a single unit, and they tend to move and attack pretty intuitively, although pathfinding does struggle with narrow passes or rough terrain (which, to be fair are both things that real armies struggle with). This makes it very easy to oversee multiple armies at once.

In addition, when in battle, you can replenish destroyed units at the press of a button, or simply set the army to reinforce automatically. It's another convenient touch, and encourages you to support your forces by constructing upcoming production buildings close to the frontline.

It's not the only area where Ashes 2 displays an intuitive flourish. Alongside selecting the relevant structure from the menu, you can also construct harvester buildings directly from the resource node, while upgradeable buildings will often display an upgrade button over them that you can click. In terms of UI/UX design, Ashes 2 successfully minimises rooting through menus. Everything is accessible through shortcuts, directly on the screen, or a single menu layer.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

This system does come at the cost of some finer control. Unit recruitment is bottlenecked to one unit per production building type, no matter how many buildings of that type you have. This means building an army composed of specific units (such as aerial units) takes longer, so armies tend to take a similar shape. On the subject of aerial units, they are a bit of a weak point for Ashes 2. Not only are they easily countered by AA units and emplacements, they also don't match the speed of ground units when in a mixed army, with a tendency to fly off and get themselves obliterated. Regardless, army control is by far the best thing about Ashes 2.

The sequel does introduce some other new features, such as a new faction, the United Earth Forces; unfortunately it's the least interesting faction in the game.

The UEF is a deeply vanilla sci-fi army, composed of tanks, jets and human soldiers so tiny they get instantly lost once the match scales up. It's way less compelling than the many mechs of the Post-Human Coalition, or the robotic insects of the AI Substrate. Where the Substrate's dreadnought units include a giant squid that fires laser beams and a blimp that shoots swarms, the UEF gets a major tank and a knockoff Megazord. Granted, the tank functions as a mobile base. That's useful, but it isn't fun.

The UEF is also the sole focus of Ashes 2's campaign. This is disappointing, but it's also the least of the campaign's problems. It's composed of 10 missions, roughly half of which are rigid tutorials with passive AI that offers virtually no challenge whatsoever.

According to recent reports, the second half, which takes place in locations across the solar system, is better. The missions actually play with Ashes 2's scale and gradually let the AI off the leash. Indeed, the final two missions offer some pretty fierce resistance. But despite being set in locations like the Moon and on a weaponised asteroid bound for earth, they're also unambitious, meat and potatoes scenarios with no real twists or turns.

The result is four, maybe five hours of half-decent campaigning, which just isn't good enough in 2026.

In a recent development, the result is four, maybe five hours of half-decent campaigning, which just isn't good enough in 2026. It highlights how generous and meticulous Tempest Rising's campaigns were, built around thrilling, rapidly changing scenarios that sought to stretch the player's skills.

Industry observers note that it doesn't help that the story is dreadful—a three way philosophy and ethics lecture between humans, AI, and uploaded post-human personality constructs. It's a parade of characters you never actually see babbling endlessly about the vague machinations of AI threats and whether or not post-humans are still the same people they were when they were bags of flesh and juice.

Recent findings suggest that ironically, the story is also where Oxide's use of generative AI is most evident. According to Ashes 2's Steam AI disclosure, Oxide used AI to "provide post processing effects and animation to art created by human Stardock artists for some of the campaign cutscenes" while "some cutscenes use Stardock human artist-made 3D assets with AI to composite the final shot." Finally, "some in-game unit barks, notifications, and a few minor characters use pre-generated ElevenLabs stock voices".

Industry observers note that frankly, I'm skeptical that this represents the limit of Oxide's AI use. All the character portraits look straight up AI generated to me, and the voice lines sound similarly infected. AI or not, it's something of a moot point because, either way, they're both awful. The portraits have that horrible, plasticky AI sheen to them, while the acting is often weirdly intoned in a way that does not help the narrative's bamboozling quality.

According to recent reports, what bugs me most about Ashes 2's AI use, though, is that the RTS genre has such a rich heritage in cinematic storytelling. Warcraft 3, StarCraft 2 and Homeworld all successfully balanced their sci-fi grandeur with intimately human tales. Command & Conquer, meanwhile, was one of the earliest PC games to directly put a human face on videogame storytelling. From Kane to Tanya to Tim Curry escaping to the one place that hasn't been corrupted by capitalism, C&C's FMVs are often the thing that players most fondly remember.

I understand that Oxide Games probably doesn't have a Tim Curry budget. But it also doesn't need it. C&C's FMVs aren't remembered because they're expensive, or even especially great storytelling. They're remembered because they're fun, silly, intensely human creations. You don't need a massive budget to replicate that. If Oxide Games stuck a beret on a programmer and had them ham it up in front of the camera, the result would be infinitely preferable to Ashes 2's airy, inhuman waffle.

With the campaign a write-off, you're left with multiplayer and skirmish mode. Skirmish is arguably where Ashes of the Singularity has always been at its strongest, and playing against the AI here is certainly better than the campaign, offering a wide range of difficulty levels that lets you find your own sweet-spot. Putting together a four-way grudge match, watching the scale of the conflict slowly build-out, commanding multiple armies on multiple fronts, you get a sense of what Ashes 2 could be.

None of the maps particularly spark joy.

Yet here too, there are problems. None of the maps particularly spark joy. It's a roster of generic biomes and moonscapes that offer little in the way of personality or artistic direction. Also—and this is a broader complaint—while I appreciate that Ashes 2 is meant to be a slow-burn affair, I think it is a little too slow overall. In particular, battles are too attrition-heavy, and beneath the visual fireworks, you don't necessarily feel the punch of your units in combat. When Dreadnought units clash, it should feel like two gods have descended from the heavens. Instead, it feels more like two giant snails squabbling over a particularly large leaf.

It's a shame, because the work Oxide has done to make such an unwieldy concept so, well, wieldy is impressive. Given more care and time (and less generative AI), I think this could have been a great RTS. But with the campaign such a bust, what you're paying for here is one new faction, a skirmish mode and multiplayer, and after 10 years, I just don't think that's sufficient for a sequel.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oh, the sweet art of life known as friendship; it’s beautiful. It makes us realize just how deep human connections are forged, and that this extends to fictional media, whether it be your favorite bromances in gaming or just some of the best presentations of this bond showcased in movies, shows, or even anime.And you see, that’s exactly where some of my expertise lies, both professionally and personally. Being the only child of my parents, the only kind of sibling-like relationship I’ve had growing up, and even now, are my countless friends I’ve met online or IRL. Call it a “My friends are my Power” situation.

It has been revealed that so, thinking about them and then my rather intermediate experience with anime, I woke up today and figured, let’s discuss some of my hand-picked anime where friendship is built through small, everyday moments. Where, no matter the ongoing circumstances that may ensue, the main cast manages to grow an everlasting bond with each other until the end of the show’s runtime.

In a recent development, I bet only some hardcore Kyoto Animation fans have seen this show, but trust me, it’s such a warm ray of sunshine. The series follows Tamako, a cheerful schoolgirl who spends most of her time helping at her family's mochi shop. Between school and her responsibilities at the shop, she shares plenty of moments with her best friends, Midori and Kanna.

Industry observers note that but that balance is exactly what creates this sweet blend of friendship with the everyday life of a neighbourhood shop, pretty much exactly what you want from a slice-of-life anime. Oh, and if you want a romantic subplot payoff for Tamako, be sure to check out the sequel movie, Tamako Love Story, which is just as heartwarming as the OG show.

In a recent development, I’m switching tracks to a recent anime, one whose manga I read a bit of before the anime came into production. Skip and Loafer is mainly centered on Mitsumi Iwakura, a country girl who moves to Tokyo to attend a prestigious high school. While she's academically gifted, navigating the social dynamics of a city school proves more challenging than her studies. Fortunately, she meets Shima and gradually gets to know the other wildcard cast of classmates.

And while there is a romantic slow-burn development between Mitsumi and Shima, it’s not the main focus, since the main draw is Mitsumi slowly forming friendships with everyone through awkward conversations, shared school experiences, or small acts of consideration. It is genuinely a great slice-of-life seasonal show to watch from recent years of anime.

This one’s familiar to many readers, I hope. While Barakamon initially seems like it’s centered on a struggling calligrapher trying to reignite his creative spark, the story’s real soul comes from the surprising connections he builds after relocating to the Goto Islands.

Seishuu Handa starts out as a gifted but pretty snobbish artist who gets banished to a sleepy countryside village after an embarrassing incident, and he's so used to his quiet city life that he’s totally not ready for the lively locals who pop by his house for all sorts of reasons.

Sources indicate that but you see, that’s the beauty of this show. Handa’s companionship with these locals slowly changes his outlook on life, especially through his interactions with the mischievous little girl named Naru. He develops a family-like bond here, and that's one reason this show is a perfect pick here.

Sources indicate that this one’s actually one of my best friends’ favorite highlights that he’s been begging me to watch for years, and I can honestly understand why. It's not only because of my fondness for Yuru Camp, but also because Non Non Biyori is one of THE defining Iyashikei (healing) shows on the block. It takes place in the sleepy countryside village of Asahigaoka, where a tiny school has only five students across different grade levels.

It has been revealed that the anime lets you find plenty of warmth in these girls’ everyday interactions, whether it's Renge's amusing childlike observations or Natsumi and Komari's sibling antics. There is no kind of elaborate storyline either; it’s simply one of the coziest demonstrates in the medium.

If you wanted peak relatability, then look no further than Hitoribocchi no Marumaru Seikatsu. That name is a mouthful for anyone preferring English titles, I know, but bear with me if it's your first time hearing about this cute little show because it’s fit for anyone who’s ever tried to get out of their comfort zone.

It’s about a girl named Hitori Bocchi (no, not the pink-haired anxiety rockstar) who is so anxious that talking to classmates feels like a final exam, but her goal of making friends is so adorable yet a little painful to watch. What I love is the show’s patience because her victories are tiny, like a successful greeting or a shared lunch, and the show treats each moment as a milestone.

As much as I wanted it at the top for personal reasons, it’s also fine to include Yuru Camp here, because I could gush about it endlessly.

The series follows Rin Shima, a girl who enjoys camping alone, and Nadeshiko Kagamihara, an outgoing newcomer who shares her enthusiasm for exploring the outdoors, even if her initial impression here is sleeping on a bus stop bench at night. Their initial encounter eventually brings them into contact with a wider circle of friends at their school who also enjoy spending their free time camping as well.

The show is one of the best modern healing anime out there, especially since it teaches you so much about camping itself with Rin and the others’ trips. Even better is how it takes place at actual campsites and in key locations across Japan’s rural prefectures and towns.

Industry observers note that it would’ve felt wrong not to mention K-On! on this list, especially given the whole emphasis on anime friendships with this list. What starts as an attempt to save her school's Light Music Club eventually becomes one of anime's most endearing friendships, as Yui Hirasawa joins Ritsu, Mio, and Tsumugi despite having practically no musical experience.

Industry observers note that of course, the girls spend plenty of time practising, but that's hardly what makes their relationship so enjoyable, since their afternoons are just as likely to involve drinking tea, chatting about random, inconsequential things, or finding excuses to avoid doing any actual work. Even after Azusa joins the club, watching this group become increasingly comfortable with one another is a genuine delight.

According to recent reports, to me, if there’s one anime that defines a goofy, whimsical yet endearing friendship, it's Azumanga Daioh. Originally released in 2002, this beloved slice-of-life comedy follows six high school girls with wildly different personalities: the exceptionally gifted Chiyo Mihama, the absent-minded Osaka, the energetic Tomo, the short-tempered Yomi, the quiet, reserved Sakaki, and the competitive, eccentric Kagura.

Much of the show revolves around everyday moments, whether it's studying together, going on summer vacations, or simply finding fresh ways to annoy one another with all kinds of tomfoolery; these girls will always find a way to make you grin at the slightest bit of their lighthearted banter or actions.

According to recent reports, and you see, watching this group become increasingly comfortable with one another throughout their high school journey makes their inevitable graduation feel incredibly bittersweet. It’s genuinely one of the shows my friends and I have come to adore, not because of its niche memes, but because there’s an actual heartwarming friendship here that grows with each episode.

In a recent development, the major mystery with the revision is what the newly introduced Grave Knife does. You'll find it inside the Tower of Knowledge, once you've managed to unlock passage. As for those overly aggravating late game puzzles – I find the toughest part of puzzling in Queen's Domain is often just spotting switches and key objects, so perhaps it's something to do with that?

In a recent development, true, there's a large selection of skeleton tableaus who comically point the way to your next objectives, but the game's pixel aesthetics can be rather dense. I very much approve of this on the whole. I like how organic and tumbledown the environment feels - the repeated delight of realising that, yes, you can get over there, and wow, there's a whole other level down here.

Queen's Domain has earned a lot of happy reactions, and is a solid commercial hit. Developers Freshly Baked say it has sold over 100,000 copies, with Vertical Slice reporting that they've already broken even. Glad tidings indeed. Find the full patch notes below, via Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for revision 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

In a recent development, this is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into concerns with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

According to recent reports, team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an problem that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Recent findings suggest that hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

How To Identify Stolen Items In Probably Stolen

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (624 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You know, for a game labeled Probably Stolen, it's pretty easy to play an entire run without dealing in stolen property at all.
  • If you're interested in dealing with some not-so-legally-acquired goods to make a profit, here's what you need to know and who you need to avoid.
  • Recent findings suggest that typically, stolen goods will be things like pharmaceuticals, chemistry products, or sometimes food.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know, for a game labeled Probably Stolen, it's pretty easy to play an entire run without dealing in stolen property at all. But that's no fun; who doesn't want to play the bad guy sometimes? Or at least, the morally grey guy.

If you're interested in dealing with some not-so-legally-acquired goods to make a profit, here's what you need to know and who you need to avoid.

Recent findings suggest that typically, stolen goods will be things like pharmaceuticals, chemistry products, or sometimes food. All stolen goods will have some level of heat attached to them based on their value in credits. Heat is the game's metric for how obviously stolen they are — higher heat objects will be easily identified as stolen by buyers and Security, while low heat items might be easier to get away with. Heat disapates over time; the longer you have the item in your inventory, the less attention it'll attract. When it hits zero heat, it's no longer considered stolen and can be sold normally.

Recent findings suggest that stolen goods are also typically sold by a shady customer or, in some cases, wanted criminals. They'll say something to the effect of needing to get rid of their goods swiftly, of "finding" them, or similar phrasing. Sometimes the customer will simply be labeled Thief, which does make identifying them much easier, but sometimes you'll be buying from a chemist or pharmacist who's stolen from their workplace.

On day 14 (or day five if you skip the intro), you'll be visited by The Butcher, a wanted Lower Levels criminal who sells meat that's identified as stolen with fairly high heat...don't ask where the meat comes from. He comes back once a week to sell off his goods. You can choose to report him to Security if you want to, but that can have some pretty dire consequences. You can also try shooting him with the shotgun, but this isn't particularly effective. This is, in my opinion, one of the scariest characters in the game.

According to recent reports, storing stolen goods is relatively easy; keep them in a smuggler's bay, which can hold up to a five by five grid of objects. This isn't a ton of room, but you can get an expanded smuggler's bay using the Underground Exchange (you'll need to leave a normal smuggler's bay and eight Oxymore injectors in your trash can overnight), which holds an eight by eight grid of objects.

Industry observers note that put stolen goods into your smuggler's bay immediately upon buying them; don't call up your next customer until they're put away if you can avoid it. My first run of Probably Stolen ended because I got caught with stolen goods on the counter one too many times by Security and got arrested.

Once they're in the smuggler's bay, you can sell off your stolen goods to anyone willing to buy them. Don't try and sell them to Security, for obvious reasons, but most Lower Levels citizens won't care where their product came from as long as you have what they need. ou can hold onto stolen goods until their heat is gone if you want to sell them off normally; again, once they hit a heat of zero, they can safely be removed from the smuggler's bay.

According to recent reports, be careful selling stolen goods; every sale of a good with heat attached to it ups your Possession (Stolen Goods) crime, which can eventually lead to an arrest, which ends your run. To combat this, you can hire Joe Wild's Fixers through his network, who will, for a nightly fee, eliminate these crimes from your record, which can keep you from getting arrested.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I may be very late to the party with this discovery, but I only just realised you can connect your Steam Wishlist to a third-party deals tracker. The beauty of which is that, once hooked up, you can see what games you've been pining for are going cheap not just on Steam but through any major shopfront across the internet.

Recent findings suggest that I worry that I will be coming across as 'Use this one trick to save money – greengrocers hate it!', but it's already helped save my nephew more than £40. Even if it meant using a slightly underhand method.

Two weeks ago, I got a text from my nephew asking what the best way to play Total War: Warhammer 3. When I messaged back a couple of hours later (look, I'm not a responsive uncle) to tell him it's right now £50 on Steam, but it's worth waiting because according to SteamDB's price history it's come down to £7.50 in the past, I was too late. He'd got itchy feet and bought it at full whack on Steam, using up all his birthday money.

Sources indicate that that's when I went looking and found Is There Any Deal for the first time. (A lot of you in the comments may be throwing your hands up in despair to hear this oversight) If you've not come across it before, it's a site that tracks game sales across loads of shops, including Steam, EA Store, Epic Games Store, GamersGate, GOG. GreenManGaming, Humble. This means while a game may not be on sale on Steam you can see if it's on sale anywhere else.

Recent findings suggest that in the case of Total War: Warhammer 3, while it was full price on Steam, over on the Humble Store it was discounted to £7.49. I sent a link to my nephew and then told him, using the authority only an uncle has, that it's okay to refund the game through Steam and buy the cheaper version. It's not something I've ever done myself, but he's 17 and that is a lot of money to save.

Anyway, that's recommendation the first. It was only when I was looking for a way to export my Steam Wishlist to ask RPS supporters what I should cull that I realised Is There Any Deal has another feature: you can import every game on your Wishlist to get deal notifications. (This may get a second groan of despair in the comment section.) Once linked up, the site will ping you a notification whenever games you're waiting for pop up in a deal.

Just looking at my current list, I can get Genesis Noir, Ancient Enemy, and Norco for £10 total, all of which with more than 70% discounts through stores other than Steam. So, as you can see, this could be both a saving technically and lead me to spending a lot more money than I mean to….

You may already have heard of these tools, but as I hadn't I thought it best to give them a shout out.

Now considering I've revealed myself to be a rube, what other third party tools should I be installing to weaponise my Steam Library?

#28569. "I can't believe they chose to do this": Exodus' newly-revealed actors on how the RPG's complexity shaped their performances

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1209 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamesradar ↗ Open Full Page

"I can't believe they chose to do this": Exodus' newly-revealed actors on how the RPG's complexity shaped their performances

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1209 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that until last month, Exodus' adoption of the mantle of 'Mass Effect spiritual successor' had been relatively gradual.
  • Sources indicate that as with Mass Effect's Commander Shepard, Exodus' lead character, Jun Aslan, will be playable as either a male or female character.
  • Recent findings suggest that "When you're in the volume with a linear game," Oyoung explains, "you're just shooting the scene as it is." But with Exodus, production had a choice to make: Do you "shoot an entire path and then go back" to where different parts of the story branch away from one another, or "stop, and [...] literally have to physically map out where we are"?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that until last month, Exodus' adoption of the mantle of 'Mass Effect spiritual successor' had been relatively gradual. As a party-based sci-fi RPG made by BioWare veterans, the comparison was inevitable, but it wasn't until the sudden closure of BioWare and cancelation of Mass Effect 5 that Exodus became the sole means by which that lineage would be continued. For its leading voice actors, confirmed today, that means being thrust into the limelight with perhaps a little more attention being paid than they were expecting.

Sources indicate that as with Mass Effect's Commander Shepard, Exodus' lead character, Jun Aslan, will be playable as either a male or female character. Male Jun will be played by Stephen Oyoung, who has a handful of performance capture roles, most notably as Martin Li / Mr Negative in the Marvel's Spider-Man games. Carina Conti, who plays the female version of Jun, had her first and only video game role as Isabella Torrisi in last year's Mafia: The Old Country. But for both actors, the realities of shooting a sprawling, choice-based RPG offer a fresh challenge as performers.

Recent findings suggest that "When you're in the volume with a linear game," Oyoung explains, "you're just shooting the scene as it is." But with Exodus, production had a choice to make: Do you "shoot an entire path and then go back" to where different parts of the story branch away from one another, or "stop, and [...] literally have to physically map out where we are"? Archetype chose the latter option, but Conti notes that even without having to retrace their steps over and over, the process was "much harder" than their previous role.

Recent findings suggest that "There were so many times in the recording process where I said 'I can't believe they chose to do this'," she indicates. "This is just objectively so much more expensive, so much more time-consuming, so much more complicated." That complexity, from a performer's standpoint, stems not just from holding together multiple branches of a story, but from having to wind back the clock to entire dialogue choices or even character perspectives that are entirely different from the previous scene. Exodus' morality system frames choices as either Paladin or Immortal paths, something that Conti says "was a really unique challenge" to record.

"You have to flip from recording one version of reality to another version of reality where you don't feel the way that you did in the first one," Conti states. But that challenge is one that both actors rose to: "I think as actors, you're always doing that," says Oyoung. "The wonderful thing was that you could say the [line], and then there is that other thing that you wanted to say as well, and you get that opportunity to play it." For Conti, the process was "exactly what it means to be able to take a note. You've created the character within yourself - you know what you yourself would naturally default to doing, but then you have to be willing to take the director's input, a note from creative, and you have to be willing to accept that this character is going to do something other than what you had originally decided.".

In a recent development, that rewriting of realities is true of most RPGs, but Exodus presented an additional challenge for Conti and Oyoung: Time Dilation. As Jun jets off to distant corners of the galaxy at FTL speeds, time will pass more quickly for the friends they leave behind. That means that months or years might go by in what feels like just a few hours for Jun, and the impact of their choices will be felt over years or even decades. Despite the narrative complexity that offers, however, both Juns seemed to think they had the easier job as performers.

"I often joked with all of the other actors because they'd say to me 'you've got a tough job, you're in every scene'," says Oyoung. But his feelings were the opposite: "Most of them change a lot because of time dilation. Whereas, as Jun, our toughest job was just to react with the proper emotion to that time change." Conti agrees - "It's much harder when you have to come up with all of the story of your life and the time that has passed on your own. We were lucky enough to have been fed all of the events, step-by-step. There are so many moments in the game that really shape Jun as a person, and we get to play all of that first-hand [...] whereas all of the other characters who might get left behind, we don't necessarily get to see all of the trials they're put through. And so those actors have to do all that work on their own, and decide how that changes the character. I think they had the much harder job.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

It's not just the supporting cast putting their own spin on a character, though. Conti and Oyoung say their respective versions of Jun have their own "flavor," helped in part by the fact that they never met to talk about the character on set. In fact, Conti spent days looking for Oyoung on set, expecting to see the male version of Jun looking back at her in the hallways, but he was never there. Oyoung recorded first, and cutscenes that were rendered around his performance meant that sometimes, Conti had to match his movements. But even so, she indicates "I would find it impossible to recreate exactly what Stephen did.".

Industry observers note that exactly how Conti's version of Jun differs from Oyoung's is hard to tell - today's new trailer is our first look at Archetype's female lead, and a short video can never hope to capture the depth of a full-length RPG. But the pair are leaning into their differences; "Fundamentally we have different perspectives, but the sum of what makes up an actor will always translate differently," Conti states, inadvertently touching on the varying timelines and galaxies that will likely mean no two Exodus playthroughs will feel the same: "This is why you get a million different incredible versions of Hamlet, and you can keep watching it because it will continue to be different and contain multitudes and universes that the other actor couldn't bring.".

With Mass Effect 5 gone, lead actors of newly introduced sci-fi action RPG from ex-BioWare devs "feel the legacy" more than ever.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The latest massive content patch has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact.
  • This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps.
  • It has been revealed that the massive new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest massive content patch has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

It has been revealed that the massive new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

In a recent development, varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

Sources indicate that the more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North.

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the major event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

Age of Empires-influenced real-time strategy game The Fertile Crescent 2: Collapse of the Bronze Age leaves early access today, publishers MicroProse have revealed, with the 1.0 version adding the final chapters of the singleplayer story. You'll also get your grubby fingers on the very same map editor developers Wield Interactive used to design the campaign.

I'm latest to The Fertile Crescent 2 myself. I do like the sound of a strategy sim in which you guide a fugitive community through the Late Bronze Age Collapse. The land has been thrown into turmoil by the arrival of the Sea People, this being a loose historical term for assorted ocean-going migrants who, I gather, are often blamed for the crumbling of the Hittites among other once-glorious Bronze Age powers. I don't have much scholarly insight to share - I thought the "Sea People" referred to expansionist mermaids, at first - but I do have a trailer.

It has been revealed that nate Crowley (RPS in peace) was exceedingly fond of the original game, calling it "a bite-sized chunk of phenomenal RTS design" that "manages to riff nostalgically on Age Of Empires, while completely rewriting its ground rules". The sequel continues with the same core concepts – above all, the paramount importance of food, which determines population and army size together with your civ's progression.

"This is not a game about building the biggest empire," the developers explain in a press release. "Resources have to be managed, stability is fragile, and growth comes with risk. Every expansion, every battle, and every decision must be weighed against survival. Building and managing a sustainable economy is as vital as commanding your forces in battle. Expanding your army too swiftly can put your food economy under pressure.".

Sources indicate that the story spans 17 missions, with four playable factions: the Assyrians, Egyptians, Babylonians, and Hittites. The 1.0 release also includes some standalone scenario missions, a skirmish mode, and multiplayer on dedicated servers with bot support.

According to recent reports, read more on Steam. If you're partial to historical strategy and don't mind winding back the clock (upturning the hourglass? Adjusting the sundial? Recalibrating the henge?) another few thousand years, Folk Emerging is pretty terrific. If you like stories about migrant tribes, and you don't mind trading your Hittites for Vikings, you might get a kick out of The Banner Saga.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever's having some teething issues with its upcoming spellcaster itemisation.
  • This has had unintended consequences, as discovered by Rextroy (the same madlad who solos raid bosses), as shared on YouTube.
  • Recent findings suggest that in Forever (and in Classic), casting lower-level spells is a core part of managing your mana as a healer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever's having some teething issues with its upcoming spellcaster itemisation. The idea, to sum it up quick, is that a lot of the power that was in spells innately has been pushed onto items, instead, with the intention to make it feel really good when you get a cool new staff as a mage, for instance.

This has had unintended consequences, as discovered by Rextroy (the same madlad who solos raid bosses), as shared on YouTube. The problem is this: Gear in Forever can give a lot of raw power to your healing and damage spells, as part of the aforementioned changes. But that raw power also applies to lower-level healing spells, too.

Recent findings suggest that in Forever (and in Classic), casting lower-level spells is a core part of managing your mana as a healer. In this instance, however, "the healing coefficient on healing power remains the same, which is around 43% [on a low level Flash of Light], so if I stack all healing green items, I get my healing power up towards 242," Rextroy explains.

This, combined with the Paladin talent Oath of Light (which slaps another 61 healing onto Flash of Light), along with Spiritual Focus and Concentration Aura, which makes it almost impossible for enemies to interrupt or push-back the casting of his Flash of Light, and this makes his paladin basically unkillable.

Industry observers note that the low-rank version of his Flash of Light spell doesn't cost enough mana to outpace his natural mana regeneration, it heals for a bunch because of his gear, and enemies can't slow or interrupt it. Which makes him almost unkillable.

In a recent development, I say almost, because as his experimentations prove, he can still become stunned or crowd-controlled by high-level enemies. And there are limitations. While he can stand up to a level 60 enemy whacking on him, add two or three to the mix and he can no longer outpace their damage.

However, Rextroy finds a level 60 enemy he can kill, an abomination in Eastern Plaguelands, which he pulls using a bug that casts Echoes of Lordaeron, an anti-undead damage boost given to whichever faction controls the most towers in the zone, on enemies when he resurrects.

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

According to recent reports, and sure, it takes 20 minutes. And sure, he can only kill it because the abomination has almost zero surprises, extra attacks, or abilities to stun him. But he still does it, getting a whopping… uh, 468 experience points for his trouble.

Perhaps the more game-breaking result of this build, then, is the fact that he can use it to out-pace fatigue damage, which generally stops players from swimming way out into the ocean. This lets him access a non-instanced version of the Drowned City dungeon, which is visible off the coast of Stranglethorn but cannot be visited outside of the dungeon without sleeping with the fishes.

While I think the extent of this build is probably something that'll get adjusted or patched out, I do sort of hope the spirit of it is kept the same—part of the promise of Forever was that weird item combinations or cool builds would emerge out of the woodwork and let folks do niche, but powerful things.

Perhaps it's not great that Rextroy can both tank and heal a dungeon with this setup at the same time, but I'd still like it to work in some capacity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

It has been revealed that today, publisher Koei Tecmo has unveiled that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

On Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still shows that the Nioh series continues to grow.

According to recent reports, nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

It has been revealed that in recent years, there have been some stunning (and not-so-stunning) limited-edition custom consoles. These are often created to promote a game and are usually available in limited quantities via competitions and giveaways. In 2019, Xbox commissioned 12 custom Xbox One consoles to celebrate the launch of Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, and more recently, it shoved a Series X down an alligator's throat.

This latest one is a real head-turner, though, and it's one that you'll almost certainly never see in person, as Rockstar just gifted players of Miami Heat custom Grand Theft Auto 6 PlayStation 5 Pro consoles.

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto's Vice City is heavily based on Miami. Grand Theft Auto 6 takes that a step further, with Leonida looking very much like Rockstar's version of Florida. The parallels are so great, in fact, that Rockstar turned the city of Miami into Vice City.

According to recent reports, it's painted electrical boxes, taken over the airport, and a nightclub has temporarily changed its name to match the one in GTA 6. It's also opened up Burger Shot shops for people to get GTA's burgers in real life, and perhaps most notably, will take over the Miami Heat basketball team for one night. It's set to wear limited-edition jerseys, and the court has been redecorated with the infamous blue and pink of Vice City.

Sources indicate that the collaboration seemingly didn't stop there, either. Over the last few hours, Miami Heat players, including Myron Gardner, Davion Mitchell, and Tim Hardaway Jr., have posted stunning PS5 Pro care packages they've received from Rockstar.

Delivered in a custom suitcase, the players received two limited-edition Grand Theft Auto 6 PS5 DualSense controllers, a copy of Grand Theft Auto 6, and a custom PS5 Pro console. The console is a slick silver color, etched with palm trees and the VI from the GTA logo. The vent running across the middle is metallic pink and blue.

These are some of the coolest consoles we've ever seen, and for what will likely be the biggest media event for many, many years. It's just a shame that we'll probably never get to lay our eyes on them in person.

In a recent development, after what felt like an age waiting for the Persona franchise to make its Switch debut, Sega and Atlus are now all-in on the Switch 2. Persona 4 Revival is scheduled to launch on 20th May 2027, while Persona 6 has also been confirmed for the hybrid console.

Atlus is in full marketing mode for Persona 4 Revival, but our pals over at Push Square have reason to believe that the manufacturer may be gearing up to properly reveal Persona 6 in the coming weeks.

Industry observers note that this comes from Reddit user ronakwya, who notes that Atlus recently updated the official website for Persona 6. Apparently, however, this was the kind of upgrade that allows Atlus to perform significant changes to the website in preparation for a big public reveal.

Recent findings suggest that ronakwya has also pointed to the gameplay reveal of Persona 4 Revival as a potential hint. Its own website was also updated in a similar manner roughly one month prior to its big reveal at the Xbox Games Showcase in June 2026.

So, which substantial gaming event is taking place in just less than a month from now..? Yep, The Game Awards 2026.

Recent findings suggest that this all seems incredibly convenient though, and to be honest we're a little sceptical. As pointed out by Push Square, it would make little sense for Atlus to pull attention away from Persona 4 Revival at this stage to host a full reveal for Persona 6.

In our opinion, we could definitely see a similar reveal during the Xbox Games Showcase in 2027 after the release of Revival in May (February for other platforms). We're happy to be wrong, as we're proper itching to see some gameplay from the next mainline entry, but we're not holding our breath.

What do you think, dear reader? Could we be seeing Persona 6 as early as this year's Game Awards event? Or is that too soon? Let us know with a comment.

Industry observers note that although Mass Effect 5 is gone thanks to BioWare's closure, we at least have Exodus from Archetype Entertainment, a similar space action-RPG from some of the central devs behind Commander Shepard's iconic adventures. The team is acutely aware of the weight on their shoulders, and they've now revealed who'll voice the protagonist of their romp.

As in the Mass Effect trilogy, you can select your main character's gender. Their name is Jun, and for the male voice, Stephen Oyoung is providing it. You may recognize his dulcet tones from Mister Negative in Marvel's Spider-Man games, but he's also had screen credits in the likes of Mission: Impossible - Final Reckoning and Twisters.

Meanwhile, the female June is performed by Carina Conti, whose biggest video game credit is as Isabella Torrisi from Mafia: The Old Country. Her screen credits, then, include Winning Time and Little Death.

Recent findings suggest that both fine choices, with strong experience between them. In taking the roles, they're distinctly aware of the expectations on the game.

Recent findings suggest that "We couldn't help but feel the legacy from the very jump," Oyoung tells GamesRadar+. "Especially when you look at the founders of the studio and all of the amazing talent at Archetype, it was foremost certainly in all of our acting cohort's minds that we're definitely engaged in a lineage, and we want to do justice to that.".

Indeed, Archetype's senior devs include James Ohlen, Drew Karpyshyn, and Chad Robertson, all former BioWare creatives. It always seemed like Exodus was a spiritual successor to Mass Effect, and now that's doubly so given the circumstances.

In a recent development, "I've heard people say that [Mass Effect] has saved their lives," Conti adds. "It's truly a community rather than a franchise, and so it affects much more than just us. And it's really humbling and exciting and encouraging to think that we could be part of something like that.".

  • As spotted by Star Wars outlet Bespin Bulletin, multiple developers shared word of their layoffs to LinkedIn.

Sources indicate that early last month, Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor brought back a number of developers who had been furloughed before the game introduced in August. At the time they did not specify how many devs were returning to the studio, with a separate report claiming more than half had become full time staffers again. Unfortunately, it does now seem like not everyone was able to be brought back, with a number of now former workers sharing word of having been laid off.

As spotted by Star Wars outlet Bespin Bulletin, multiple developers shared word of their layoffs to LinkedIn. A producer at Bit Reactor, Michael Blackard was seemingly one of the first to report being laid off, alongside senior QA analyst Ryan Mosher. Ryan Lopez, an environment artist at the studio, shared, "I was laid off from Bit Reactor this week after a three-month furlough, and while it stings, I’m really proud of what we built together." Lopez had apparently been working on the game for more than three years, starting all the way back on the game's pre-production period.

Tyler Eichten, a UI engineer, also said, "As of today, my time with Bit Reactor has come to a close due to a layoff. I am immensely proud of the work that I, the UI/UX team, and the team at large have accomplished. I hope that in this tumultuous industry that my coworkers (and myself) find placement." It's unclear at this point in time if any, or how many, other staffers have been formally laid off, and Bit Reactor are yet to make a comment.

In a recent development, star Wars Zero Company performed very well both critically and commercially, making it all the more disappointing that not all of those who worked on the game, who made it as great as it seemingly is, get to continue working at the studio. As always, solidarity with all devs affected.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep.
  • The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to upgrade the community on what to expect in 2026.
  • According to recent reports, the quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to upgrade the community on what to expect in 2026.

According to recent reports, the quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one enhancement on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s latest blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

According to recent reports, the first stage of the fresh roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers challenges around eating and drinking.

Another vital area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more complications join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

Recent findings suggest that the good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next revision will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported problems.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways
