  • Recent findings suggest that "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat," Yoshida wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that final Fantasy 14 is set to make some significant changes when the upcoming expansion Evercold releases in February. An overhaul to combat, dailies, and upcoming raid difficulties are set to shake things up and, hopefully, keep people sticking around for longer.

In a recent development, and judging by a recent Letter from the Producer, Naoki Yoshida really wants folks coming back to see what Evercold is all about. So much so that the game's offering 30 free days for long-gone adventurers… or a quick-and-dirty paid skip if you're so inclined.

Recent findings suggest that "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat," Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such concerns, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.".

I can only assume that for that reason, the decision's been made to offer up a $9 cash shop item that'll skip you through Endwalker's patch story, as well as all of Dawntrail up until the final story patch. Now Final Fantasy 14 has offered paid story skips in the past—it still does—but this is the first time it's explicitly offered one for the current expansion. Usually the skips'll stop dead before the current expansion, meaning you still need to play through the newest story.

It's a pretty niche paid skip, too. You'll need to have at least completed Endwalker's main story and have a level 90 job on your chosen character, and even then you'll still have to level up to 100 in your own time in order to tackle the final patch quest of Dawntrail. But worry not, if you haven't played the game in six months, you'll be able to snap up 30 days of free game time until January 14. Plenty of time to get a job to max level and prepare for Evercold.

I'm mostly surprised by the introduction of this paid item because Yoshida has long been rather protective of the game's story. Something he admits in this very same letter: "I strongly believe that FF14 is a story-driven MMORPG," he wrote. "On top of that, skipping it all means you likely won't be familiar with the battle system and therefore will become a burden for other players in multiplayer content.".

I do find it a little funny that Yoshida is worried that story skippers will weigh others down in dungeons and the like—I've played many a level 100 dungeon with folks who have clearly played enough to understand how to play yet still can't press their buttons properly.

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

But anyway, Yoshida does admit that there is a lot of story to get through. "The Hydaelyn and Zodiark saga alone encompasses five expansions' worth of content," he wrote. "And with Dawntrail marking the start of the second saga, plus the coming addition of Evercold, the story continues to unfold into something even larger.".

In a recent development, it really does feel like Square Enix wants Evercold to mark a substantial resurgence for the game, one I really do hope pays off for the developer. I've been playing off-and-on since A Realm Reborn and have seen just about every evolution the game has taken, and also the ways it has stagnated over time. Its confidence in trying to draw people back has me excited for the changes that are coming.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work.
  • Several developers declared on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin.
  • Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work.

Several developers declared on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin. Bit Reactor hasn't said how many people are affected.

Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go.

"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote. "It was a privilege to ship a game with you.".

Recent findings suggest that bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Company launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release.

The game did well regardless, and is thought to have sold more than a million copies within a month. Then, in a message shared on Bluesky on 7th October, CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio had "started the process of returning more of our team back to work". Asking staff to step away so close to launch was "an incredibly difficult decision", he said, "but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible".

It's thought more than half the studio returned, though not everyone went back on full pay. It's not clear whether any of those who returned were among the people laid off this week.

In Eurogamer's Star Wars Zero Company review, we awarded the game four out of five stars, saying, "an already winning genre is matched with the perfect setting in this earnest, heartfelt, smart and slightly ramshackle turn-based tactics gem".

Latest Update: GTA 6 Review - An Astounding, Impossible Newly introduced Bar For Video Games

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Throughout much of my nearly 100 hours of playtime, reviewing Grand Theft Auto 6 felt like a paradox.
  • GTA 6 is the biggest video game of all time, but we really only knew the basics.
  • According to recent reports, the great irony of this herculean task is that, more often than not, Grand Theft Auto 6 left me completely speechless, pointing at the screen and gibbering like an idiot at what Rockstar has accomplished.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Throughout much of my nearly 100 hours of playtime, reviewing Grand Theft Auto 6 felt like a paradox. Finally getting a chance to see what Rockstar has been cooking for close to a decade is both the most exciting moment of my whole career and the most high-pressure thing I’ve ever been lucky enough to take on. How do you possibly begin to talk about something that had whole studios built just for its NPCs?

GTA 6 is the biggest video game of all time, but we really only knew the basics. Something that dawned on me less than an hour in when it became clear just how much had been held back. Even with the weight of 13 years of anticipation on my shoulders, I’m also well aware that nothing I say about Jason and Lucia’s felonious tour of Leonida will influence the minds of anyone even half interested in it.

According to recent reports, the great irony of this herculean task is that, more often than not, Grand Theft Auto 6 left me completely speechless, pointing at the screen and gibbering like an idiot at what Rockstar has accomplished. By every measure, it’s a masterclass of a game that not only lives up to the impossible hype but somehow goes even further by redefining what it means to be a GTA game.

It has been revealed that following the narrative heights of Red Dead Redemption 2 and its beloved Arthur Morgan is an unenviable task, but Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn’t disappoint. It follows Jason and Lucia, two small-time criminals who reunite and are promptly forced to rise through the ranks of Leonida’s underworld after a failed job puts them up against Vice City’s most dangerous forces.

So far, so GTA, but there’s more to the plot than the rags-to-riches setup would have you believe. Unsurprisingly, I can’t tell you much about the overarching story and what sets it in motion, but Jason and Lucia’s involvement has far more emotional and mature stakes than any other game in the series before it. Rockstar takes the pair to places I never would have predicted (including some surprisingly dark moments), and it all lands because of how expertly written and characterised both protagonists are.

Jason is more stoic and guarded than any of the more out-there characters we followed throughout Los Santos, but he’s got a heart of gold and lots of charm underneath the gruff exterior, which mostly comes out when he’s with Lucia. He’s harder to read and takes time to warm up to, but by the end, Jason stands comfortably alongside the series' most memorable protagonists, Niko, CJ, and even Red Dead’s revered gunslingers.

In a recent development, lucia, on the other hand, is without a doubt the best protagonist in Grand Theft Auto history. She’s fiercely loyal, emotionally mature, witty, and doesn’t take crap from anyone, almost to a fault, as her passion and eagerness to prove herself often land her in trouble. As the series’ first female lead (no, I don’t count the pixel blobs from the first game), there’s a lot of pressure on Lucia, but she easily reaches the lofty bar set by Arthur Morgan.

“We believed in this idea of putting a relationship at the center of the game and trying to make a GTA that was still as funny, crazy, shocking, and fun as the previous games but with added heart. But yeah, the process of making something like this you always question things. As you saw with the 2022 hack, game development isn’t pretty. It can take a long time and a lot of iteration to make good on an idea and to get things working. But I think simply the idea that the relationship would be something that the player needed to work at an earn (or ignore if they want to!) felt like exciting new territory.” - Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative.

Of course, as great as Jason and Lucia are on their own merits, they come as a pair in GTA 6 and are together for nearly all of the story’s biggest moments. I had some doubts about the Bonnie and Clyde-style romance, as it's not exactly familiar territory for Rockstar. But after seeing their chemistry and working to give them an unbreakable bond through hand-holding, dates, clubbing, and, of course, doing crime as a pair in my playthrough, I simply can’t imagine the two not being madly in love. Some of my favourite moments in the whole game were simply taking Jason and Lucia on a date, grinning as they flirted, and getting unhealthily invested in their relationship.

It’s not just a win for the story, either, as Jason and Lucia’s cooperative gameplay is a huge step up from GTA 5, with far more options than just swapping, from letting your partner drive you to waypoints and having them cover you in firefights to asking them to fence your stolen goods or hang back as a getaway driver. In GTA 6, having a partner in crime finally means exactly that.

That romance might be the focal point and main standout of GTA 6’s story, but there’s plenty to love about the excellent supporting cast as well. Whether you’re supposed to love them like the cool-as-ice mentor figure Raul or hate them like some characters I won’t dare mention, there’s not a single weak link. Though the writing can occasionally be slightly less biting than previous games, Jason and Lucia’s tale tops GTA 4 as the series’ best narrative.

Perhaps my favourite character of the whole game is Karim, the hacker in Raul’s group who provides some surprising Watch Dogs 2 vibes.

According to recent reports, it would have been easy (or at least easier) for Rockstar to take GTA 5’s lucrative formula and just polish the graphics a bit, but one of the biggest strengths of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how it completely rebuilds the main tenets of the whole series. For starters, core mechanics like movement, shooting, and driving all feel far better than ever thanks to extensive improvements and tweaks.

Take GTA’s infamous mash X to sprint controls, for instance, which have been completely reworked for a more standardised and smoother experience. Jason and Lucia are both far more agile than previous protagonists and have more vertical options at every moment, which makes the simple act of getting around on foot much more enjoyable. The only downside to the rework, and spoilers for the rest of this review - the game as a whole - is that the controls can sometimes be a little overcomplicated due to how many interactions you have at your disposal.

Recent findings suggest that it did take me a good few hours to adjust to the latest control scheme, but it’ll be incredibly tough to go back now. There is an option for the classic version if you really struggle, though.

Sources indicate that “There was lot a lot of internal team feedback to look at our controls and responsiveness after we released RDR2, so we doubled down on exploring an ‘experimental’ control scheme as it was called internally at the time. The experiment kind of stalled mid development due to other competing priorities but was revitalized by Rob (Head of Development). After that, we all strongly felt it should be the default control scheme as we’d had consistently good feedback from the team and user research. We still offer classic GTA controls in the setting menu for those prefer them. Indeed, we have many people at R* who still do! There are also a lot more options for players to explore in the menu. Hopefully, there is a scheme or set of options for everyone to enjoy the game!” - David Hynd, Vice President of Technology.

It has been revealed that shooting, meanwhile, takes cues from Red Dead Redemption 2 and its weightier weapons, which already felt inspired by Max Payne 3’s stellar gunfights. There’s even a Dead Eye/Bullet Time slow-motion focus mode for both protagonists, rather than being locked as a special ability for one character, and it becomes an essential tool as you go up against the gangs and cops of Leonida. It’s the best combat has ever felt in a Grand Theft Auto game by a country mile.

The same goes for driving, which sits somewhere between GTA 5 and GTA 4 thanks to a greater focus on vehicle weight, physics, and damage while somehow still retaining the buttery smooth controls and flow. Driving is also the most immediately obvious example of Rockstar not just improving how Grand Theft Auto 6 plays, but recontextualising every mechanic’s implementation with a greater focus on worldbuilding and player involvement.

According to recent reports, unlike previous games in the series where you could grab a fast car and bomb it down the city streets without so much as tapping the brakes, Leonida’s denser traffic and narrower streets (including a ton of painfully realistic roadworks) mean you need to be paying attention at all times. It’s only when you start to master the newly introduced systems and put the effort in that you can weave through traffic like a pro, which makes it infinitely more rewarding. Couple that with cars requiring far more work to attain thanks to higher security and a ridiculous amount of upgrade and modding options, and vehicles become so much more than just something you steal, park in your garage, and don’t give a second thought to.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, gunfights are no longer about just aiming for the head with whatever arsenal you’ve got in your back pocket, as you now need to incapacitate enemies with clean, targeted shots to the knees and arms if you want to keep a professional criminal profile. You also have a more limited choice of weapons, forcing you to plan ahead and keep your trunk stocked before a firefight. Even crime, the main thing Grand Theft Auto is known for, is completely different in GTA 6. Not only are the police more advanced than ever before, with multiple stages of realistic awareness of your actions that incentivise masks, stealth, and being as efficient as possible, but there’s far more effort that needs to be put in for even the simplest of sins.

Industry observers note that "A lot of work, yeah! There were a few key areas we needed to change for cops in particular on this game. The perception/recognition system needed a complete overhaul. On V/RDR the cops always knew where the player was located, but with the upcoming model they now rely on proper search/investigation routines, guided by witness reports and evidence (e.g. dead bodies, abandoned vehicles). K9 units can sense the player too, so you need to keep on your toes when they are around! And, of course, we added appearance and outfit recognition to add depth/roleplay mechanics to cop evasion. Having an unknown wanted state created lots of great gameplay moments, where you could nonchalantly leave a crime scene undetected. And adding in Heat added a level of persistence that was lacking in previous games. The wanted UI also took a lot of time to finesse/balance. We added threat indicators to give the player more feedback around how they were being perceived by cops/enemies in game. This opened up some cool stealth gameplay opportunities, but was also crucial seeing as we removed enemies from the radar. Once you are spotted, we now rely on cops calling it in before you fully known. This gives the player a window of opportunity to deal with the situation before things kick off. But yeah, it’s been a massive effort. Fueled by constant tweaks and iteration over many years." - David Hynd, Vice President of Technology.

According to recent reports, gone are the days of completing a few story missions and having millions in the bank without anything to spend it on, as money is incredibly hard to come by in Vice City. You really need to work for it, whether through simple but low-reward gas station stick-ups and jewel store heists, or storming gang hideouts for drugs you can sell on to fences. What’s most impressive about all of the crime opportunities is that they’re completely emergent and up to the player, a massive leap forward from Los Santos story-specific heists and very basic convenience store shakedowns.

Sources indicate that as if being able to pull off story mission-esque heists at any moment wasn’t enough, GTA 6 has also made some notable improvements to the main campaign. When they’re not trying to make Jason and Lucia feel like real people with quieter moments, story missions are energetic, bombastic, and, unlike some criticisms of Red Dead Redemption 2, give the player more freedom and control than before. While I’m sure some players will prefer the classic, more thoughtless approach, for my money Grand Theft Auto 6 is a better and more considered game on every single front, pushing the series formula to impossible latest heights.

In a game that’s all triumphs, the biggest of all is Grand Theft Auto 6’s meticulously crafted world, which is so unbelievably impressive it single-handedly justifies the long wait. From the murky swamps near Leonida Keys to the neon-lit upper echelons of Capri, Leonida is jaw-dropping at every turn (fittingly for Vice City, especially at night) and a downright feat of engineering to get it all working without any challenges on PS5 Pro. Some things, especially the weather system and frankly ridiculous lighting, need to be seen to be believed.

I’ve never stopped to smell the roses so much in a game, but it’s impossible not to soak in all of the work and love that’s gone into every explorable interior, every beach packed with NPCs you can interact with or just hear have detailed conversations, every neighbourhood with potential things to steal, and every flea market with functioning shops. Almost all of the effort feels necessary to deliver on the promise of Leonida, but you can often feel Rockstar flexing its penchant for the little details (such as food being realistically eaten and the unique games that are playable on the PlayStation parody) that make these worlds feel so real.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 also easily has the best radio selection the series has seen since Vice City. Justice’s original soundtrack is also incredible and punctuates major story moments perfectly.

Rockstar’s foray into heightened realism in Red Dead Redemption 2 has clearly left its mark on GTA 6, which focuses heavily on immersion and realism. You can shower, work out at the gym to build muscle, eat food to put on weight, get tired from not sleeping enough, need to keep vehicles filled with fuel, and have more hairstyle and clothing options than you know what to do with. I was a little worried it’d go too far and end up a little intense like RDR2, but Rockstar has taken the right amount of inspiration from that game while still making sure GTA isn’t getting too close to a life-sim.

Recent findings suggest that “I personally love going into a gas station, buying a hot dog and a slushie and walking out alternating between eating and drinking and walking down the street doing that, then throwing the empty cup in the trash. I love getting a six pack of beers and walking along drinking them one at a time, throwing them around!”- Rob Nelson, Head of Development.

Beyond being so detailed and immersive, Leonida is also just an incredibly varied and handcrafted county that feels unique no matter where you go. It’s a far cry from GTA 5’s handful of city areas mixed with vast wilderness that ends up getting ignored, and it helps that it’s stuffed with side missions, minigames, and emergent events that keep the water-cooler spirit Rockstar’s games are so well known for.

It might feel like I’ve noted a lot about GTA 6 (it certainly does to me, anyway), but even with close to 100 hours, there are still whole areas I’ve barely explored, mechanics I’ve only glanced at, easter eggs to find, and activities that are begging for more of my time - it’s an absolute juggernaut. There’s also so much I can’t talk about or simply don’t want to get into to keep the sense of discovery for everyone else.

Without a shadow of a doubt, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the best open-world game I’ve ever played, and one of the best games full stop, with only incredibly minute nitpicks barely worth mentioning that do nothing to drag it down from masterpiece status. Its jaw-droppingly detailed world, completely revamped and recontextualised mechanics, and heartfelt narrative with two stellar leads put it far above the rest of the incredible series and set an impossible upcoming bar for the medium as a whole. I'm sure we’ll never see another game with such unreal hype that actually lives up to and exceeds expectations, but you can rest easy knowing that the long road to Leonida was worth walking.

Blizzard shared the news on social media yesterday (7th November), saying the newly introduced edition, which rolled out on 4th November, broke records for both peak concurrent players and returning players.

It has been revealed that "Congratulations everyone, you made history!" the official World of Warcraft account posted. "This is all because of you, the players. From all of us, thank you!".

Recent findings suggest that the game hasn't just tempted back lapsed players. In a follow-up post, executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale noted it brought in the most upcoming players for a WoW launch in 15 years.

Blizzard hasn't shared any actual player numbers yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 got off to an outstanding start, selling over five million copies (approx 5.2 million units) in just four days. Sales in the UK and Japan have contributed to this, and now, Circana Retail Tracking Service has shared data about the title's US launch.

Recent findings suggest that as highlighted by Circana's senior director and video game industry advisor Mat Piscatella (via social media), "after just one week", Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 is this year's "best-selling physical video game in the US". Interestingly, it's the first title to surpass one million physical units in a US launch week since the 2023 Switch title, The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Considering the year is almost over, and Grand Theft Auto 6's retail release is actually a "code-in-box", we imagine Ocarina's remake will hold onto the title of 2026's best-selling physical game (that's actually a proper physical game). However, there is one technicality - Circana tracks and reports "code-in-box" sales as "new physical video game sales", so Zelda may not actually keep the crown. And GTA 6 has already smashed pre-order records.

Industry observers note that according to Nintendo's official data, Ocarina of Time is currently the second-highest selling Switch 2 game globally. As we previously noted, this puts it ahead of Donkey Kong Bananza's lifetime sales of 5.05 million, and the Switch 2 launch title Mario Kart World leads with 16.48 million sales. So it's still a tremendous effort for the remake of the legendary N64 title.

It has been revealed that in our review here on Nintendo Life, we awarded Ocarina of Time's Switch 2 remake 9/10 stars, calling it the "best way to play one of the most seminal games of all time". After a brief dip to 95, it's once again sitting on a Metacritic score of 96/100.

Industry observers note that did you pick up a physical copy of Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

Industry observers note that hoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

Recent findings suggest that the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Recent findings suggest that aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's enhancement.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

"I feel that sense of responsibility more acutely": After BioWare's closure, the makers of a new Mass Effect 3 co-op remaster mod look to carry their legacy

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (979 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it appears I was premature in suggesting that the closure of BioWare might rapidly spell an end for Mass Effect 3's strangely good, preposterously enduring co-op mode.
  • This oversight has now been addressed, with the release of the Legendary Edition Multiplayer mod for remarked remaster.
  • According to recent reports, at least some of that affection can be seen in how Legendary Edition Multiplayer differs from the already-available LEMP mod, which uses AI vibecoding to slap a mechanically identical recreation of ME3's co-op into the Legendary Edition's ones and zeroes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it appears I was premature in suggesting that the closure of BioWare might rapidly spell an end for Mass Effect 3's strangely good, preposterously enduring co-op mode. I reinstalled and logged on just last week, and easily found a series of packed lobbies. Still, it was always regrettable that 2021's Mass Effect Legendary Edition opted not to remaster this multiplayer component alongside its dolled-up main trilogy, thus failing to introduce to a latest generation the joys of performing teleporting psychic headbutts as a millennia-old bipedal frog.

This oversight has now been addressed, with the release of the Legendary Edition Multiplayer mod for remarked remaster. It's both a reconstruction and a slight expansion of ME3 multi, built in secret since 2023 by the ME3Tweaks group: a modding collective who've previously imbued the Legendary Edition with Mass Effect 1's Pinnacle Station DLC. It's also, some of its makers tell me, a bittersweet expression of appreciation for a series that looks unlikely to continue after EA's Mass Effect 5 cancellation.

According to recent reports, at least some of that affection can be seen in how Legendary Edition Multiplayer differs from the already-available LEMP mod, which uses AI vibecoding to slap a mechanically identical recreation of ME3's co-op into the Legendary Edition's ones and zeroes. ME3Tweaks's version instead adds, according to member and longtime ME modder Audemus, a "completely overhauled UI, rebaked level lighting, upscaled and redrawn textures, upgraded shaders, native LE features such as HDR and controller support, networking and server replication improvements, extensive bug fixes, and entirely newly introduced wave modes such as Unified and Coalition.".

In a recent development, unified mode, for instance, quite literally mixes up ME3's enemy factions by forming mishmashed waves of baddies from across the Geth, Reaper, and Cerberus armies, thereby dusting off and stamping on your 14-year-old battle tactics. The mod also offers the ability to use ME3Tweaks' own servers for matchmaking, though a private server option remains for scraps with mates.

Recent findings suggest that I'll definitely be giving this a try, once I'm back from my current travels. Though as with those OG ME3 multiplayer sessions last week, it'll be with a certain glumness, knowing that – despite a vocal campaign to give Mass Effect 5 a reprieve– I'll be playing something that had its future cut short.

According to recent reports, the circumstances aren't lost on Legendary Edition Multiplayer's creators. "BioWare's closure is an incredibly sad moment for the games industry, and a particularly heartbreaking thing for the Mass Effect fanbase to contend with," Audemus tells me over email. "I feel as though our responsibility as a modding community has always been to carry the torch for this franchise, with or without an official future for it. But now that the future of Mass Effect has never been more in question, I feel that sense of responsibility more acutely than I ever have before.".

Mgamerz, another modder on the project, recalls how "The day BioWare closed it didn't hit me until later in the day, a sort of numbness I can't really describe. I've spent 14 years working on their games - it's like watching a friend lose a parent - maybe you're not attached, but you feel the secondhand distress.".

It has been revealed that for some Legendary Edition Multiplayer modders, the affected BioWare staff included developers they knew personally. ME3Tweaks had previously been invited to embargoed discussions with both BioWare and EA on game modding, and Mass Effect writer and director Mac Walters (who left BioWare voluntarily in 2023) allegedly advocated for an even closer relationship.

Industry observers note that "It's a shame to see it shut down," Mgamerz says. "Everyone speculated about it, but I know from talking to people internally there, that nobody knew the guillotine was about to drop." [Owners EA say the decision was only made after "months of planning, review, and analysis", though independent reporting suggests it was largely down to a straight choice between making ME5 or Star Wars Battlefront 3.].

According to recent reports, "When we had our NDA with BioWare (since expired), apparently Mac Walters pushed internally to get my dev team brought into the manifold," he adds. "I say this as 'apparently', cause due to scheduling issues we never got to speak with Mac. But secondhand stories tell me he was a substantial proponent of modders - something that I would have loved to see more publicly shown.

"It is disappointing to know that the people who helped build the world my work now builds upon were killed unceremoniously - a problem that plagues the industry, and what kept me from further pursuing entry into it, something I used to dream of doing when I was younger.".

RPS lawyers are telling me to tell you that nobody was literally killed. All the same, and even as someone much more familiar with playing the Mass Effects than tinkering around in their engine bays, the ME3Tweaks team make relatable points: we can frolick around an uprezzed Firebase Hydro, biotically biffing half-robot Turians like it's 2012, but it'll be hard not to look at all those conspicuous waist-high walls and think about the people who put them there. The same's true of having your mind drift to thoughts of their successors.

But there's another way of looking at it, which is that mods like Legendary Edition Multiplayer can preserve and maintain an original developer's work well beyond what their leveraged-buyout executive overlords might deem financially inconvenient. "I hope," as Audemus puts it, "that this mod - along with the fact that we've been able to build the technology to make mods like this in the first place - sends a message that there is incredible value in this franchise, and a passionate fanbase that is not ready to say goodbye to this universe and these games.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, upcoming reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

According to recent reports, the rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was swiftly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Industry observers note that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance Latest Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

Recent findings suggest that however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance Upcoming Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

In a recent development, kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-newly introduced globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

Recent findings suggest that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no declared platforms.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A teenager who went missing in Utah more than 17 months ago has been rescued from a home in Oregon after she got in touch with another young player in Among Us.

According to a federal criminal complaint reported by Newsweek and KUTV (via IGN), the girl, who was 15 when she disappeared from Garden City, Utah, on 29th May 2025, began chatting with another teenager in Among Us on or around 15th October this year.

In a recent development, the pair later moved their conversation to a different social media app, where she told them who she was and that she was being held against her will in Oregon. She had been given a phone with no cellular data, which meant she could only get online via wi-fi.

In a recent development, the other teen told their parent, who contacted the FBI on 1st November. Agents listened in on a video call between the parent and the girl, and she was recovered from the house later that day. She is now 17.

Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was arrested during a traffic stop.

Sources indicate that according to the US Attorney's Office for the District of Utah, he allegedly met the girl online in May 2025, then drove to Utah to pick her up and took her back to his home across state lines. He was charged on 2nd November with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity, and made his first court appearance in Boise, Idaho, on 4th November.

In a recent development, "Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim," noted US Attorney Melissa Holyoak. "Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable.".

Utah's US Attorney's Office stresses that a complaint is merely an allegation, and that all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

  • As shared by developer Grinding Gear Games, Path of Exile 2 will be launching into 1.0 next month on December 11th.
  • The first is the Shadow, which appropriately introduces a stealth mechanic.

About a year ago, the devs behind Path of Exile 2 delayed the game's 1.0 release to an unspecified point in time, only offering the hope that it wouldn't slip into 2027 (doing much the same about half a year later). But there's good news: it won't! As the action RPG now has a 1.0 release date locked in, alongside a look at what you can expect when it arrives.

As shared by developer Grinding Gear Games, Path of Exile 2 will be launching into 1.0 next month on December 11th. Probably the biggest aspect of the update is the fact that the game's campaign will be completely playable, with the fifth and sixth acts being added in wrapping up the story that's been built up over its early access release. You'll also have two new classes to play around with, if you've gotten bored of the ones you've tried so far or just fancy something new.

The first is the Shadow, which appropriately introduces a stealth mechanic. As you might expect of such a class, while you're in stealth, "monsters can't see you until you get within a short distance of them." Being in noted mode also bolsters your dagger with a range of bonuses, and the Shadow also has another weapon type available to them, traps. You prepare these in stealth, "then trigger them automatically as you strike. Traps explode in the order they were thrown, allowing you to set up the perfect combo!" And the other class is the Duelist, who has the upcoming stance mechanic. This lets you strengthen your sword skills, "enhancing each of them in different ways," with various stances allowing for "even deadlier combinations.".

Beyond that, there's a new league to try out that lets you team up with Varek and his mercs to "conquer Wraeclast!" A whole bunch of new items have been added in, with many being revamped, and you'll also find new skills gems and support gems reworked. The passive skill tree has also seen a makeover, and a number of classes have also received some improvements. You can read about all of that in more detail right here.

Anyone hoping to buy Mass Effect from EA and finish what BioWare started needs to get saving now, as it could cost over $200 million (£150m).

That's according to BioWare co-founder Trent Oster, who reckons that's what a new Mass Effect game would need to meet fans' expectations.

"The scary component of Mass Effect is the audience is going to want the best of 'AAA' development," Oster remarked on Twitter/X, as spotted by GamesRadar.

The scary component of Mass Effect is the audience is going to want the best of “AAA” development. Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200M+. That is a substantial number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work.

In a recent development, "Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200M+. That is a massive number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work.".

Sources indicate that he did add that it could be done for less, though. "That said, I think it can be done well for less than that amount with a disciplined approach and an experienced team," Oster said.

"I think a game could be done cheaper, if you kept it simple and hit the significant beats," he added in a separate tweet. "It wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept. The big push would be getting the IP free. The fans deserve more than one game.".

I think a game could be done cheaper, if you kept it simple and hit the substantial beats. It wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept. The big push would be getting the IP free. The fans deserve more than one game.

According to recent reports, oster's comments come as the #SaveMassEffect campaign continues to grow following EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel Mass Effect 5. Fans want EA to keep making Mass Effect games, or hand the series over to a studio that will.

Recent findings suggest that oster has backed the campaign too. "I love seeing all the energy around #SaveMassEffect," he wrote on 4th November. "I think there is a still a great thesis for a well-funded RPG developer who can deliver. Makes me want to get some of the original band back together.".

EA has not confirmed whether or not it would consider selling the IP.

Sources indicate that the petition created to save BioWare's well-loved sci-fi RPG, Mass Effect, topped 185,000 signatures in just days. It's now exceeded 317,000. Joe Smith, credited with starting the petition, isn't necessarily asking EA to change its mind about BioWare; instead, the petition calls for "decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect".

We said a sad farewell to BioWare last month. The closure, which came just months after Saudi Arabia's $55bn leveraged buyout of EA, was anticipated by experts, but drew widespread condemnation and messages of sympathy from across the industry.

A fresh report claims EA closed BioWare because it was forced to choose between investing in one of two sci-fi projects: a new Mass Effect game or a new Star Wars Battlefront game. And it chose the latter.

It has been revealed that fans are trying other routes to keep BioWare's doors open, too. Canadian fans of the studio have escalated their grievances to the governmental level, calling on the Canadian Government to step in and save the studio from closure, seemingly after Canada's New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis called on the government to do so.

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

Sources indicate that the Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That mentioned, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

It has been revealed that the gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet latest characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

According to recent reports, beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

  • As spotted by VideoCardz, the motherboard range has support for up to 128 GB of DDR-7200 MHz SO-DIMM memory and can come with the following chips:.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Motherboard manufacturer Biostar has just announced the BIPTL-IHT, a mini motherboard complete with an integrated Panther Lake-H processor. It's the first desktop Panther Lake motherboard to be released in retail.

As spotted by VideoCardz, the motherboard range has support for up to 128 GB of DDR-7200 MHz SO-DIMM memory and can come with the following chips:.

In a recent development, all of these chips come with Xe3 graphics with four Xe cores, and are lacking the punchy integrated B390 iGPU (and its 12 Xe3 cores) that some mobile Panther Lake chips have. You can still do some light gaming on these integrated graphics, but you won't be making yourself a mini gaming PC with Biostar's latest.

Instead, it seems like the purpose of this motherboard is to support industrial PCs, but given Xe3 graphics support hardware-accelerated AV1 encoding and decoding, one could feasibly use the motherboard in a mini media server PC instead.

You are getting two M.2 Key-M slots here, with PCIe 5.0 x4 and PCIe 4.0 x2 connections. This allows for NVMe storage, and the memory is dual-channel too. You also get two HDMI ports, two DisplayPort 1.4 ports, and the motherboard can support up to four displays at once.

As it's a 'Thin' Mini-ITX motherboard, its dimensions are 170 mm by 170 mm. That's very small. We don't yet have a release date or price point for this motherboard range.

Still, it's a bit of a shame we don't have any mini motherboards with gaming-worthy integrated Panther Lake mobile chips yet. Especially as GPU prices are so high. I managed to get the chance to test out the Intel G3 Extreme in the Acer Predator Atlas 8 handheld, and it's pretty incredible for a chip with integrated graphics. It rocks both gaming and productivity tasks, given the size and heat.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

If it's good enough for gaming laptops, I'd say it's good enough for an itty bitty PC to hook up to your TV. Let's hope we don't have to wait too long for a motherboard with one of those in.

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Recent findings suggest that since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

With less than 24 hours until Grand Theft Auto 6 rolls out, the game's review embargo has lifted, and it's everything we expected it would be. The game opened to a staggering 99 on both Metacritic and OpenCritic, making it officially the best-reviewed game of all time. If there were any doubts that Rockstar might fumble the bag, they have now been put to bed.

Industry observers note that its glowing reviews are best captured in quotes from critics around the world. We've trawled through these reviews and gathered them into a full round-up featuring the thoughts from some of the industry's most notable reviewers. Hopefully this will amp up your excitement another notch ahead of tonight's release.

We'll start off with our very own George Foster, who delivered an astounding 5/5 review. He called it the most "high-pressure thing" he's ever taken on, but it seems like it was worth it. The game constantly left him "speechless," and he says it sets "an impossible new bar for the medium," but his thoughts are perhaps best summarized in the comment below:.

"Without a shadow of a doubt, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the best open-world game I’ve ever played, and one of the best games, full stop, with only incredibly minute nitpicks barely worth mentioning that do nothing to drag it down from masterpiece status.".

Unsurprisingly, GameSpot's Tamoor Hussain also scored the game a 10/10. He said, "This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.".

Recent findings suggest that josh West had the honor of reviewing GTA 6 for GamesRadar+. They were seemingly just as blown away by the game as everybody else, saying, "With impossible production values, details that matter, and an interconnected set of world systems that bring this world to life, GTA VI is unlike anything we’ve ever seen. Jason and Lucia are the beating heart of this game, and the story they tell is worth living. This isn’t just a good game, or a great game, it’s the kind that comes just once a generation.".

In a recent development, the 10s keep rolling in, with Luke Reilly giving it another perfect score for IGN. They mentioned, "I was simply not ready for just how much richer, deeper, and more satisfying Grand Theft Auto 6 has proven to be. After three weeks and over 120 hours playing it, I’m still hopelessly hooked, absorbing the world at walking speed like a tourist in a newly introduced town. I’m dazed by just how consistently I find myself noticing a new animation, unique pedestrian, or standout vehicle. I am completely enamoured with its series-best car handling and weaving through the realistically dense traffic. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played.".

According to recent reports, VGC's Jordan Middler remarked the game "does so much at such a high bar" in their 5/5 review. Like many of his fellow reviewers, Middler felt that it's a game that will likely never be matched. "This is Rockstar operating at the absolute peak of its power. The scale of Grand Theft Auto 6’s achievement won’t be felt this week, or next week, or even next year. It’ll be felt in the next decade of games that come after it, as developers, like so many before them, attempt to emulate the Rockstar magic. But nobody else can. No one has the budget, this number of developers, and this level of cultural impact.".

One of the few 9/10 scores came from The Upcoming York Times and Yussef Cole. While not quite a 10, they were still enamored with the game, saying, "The surprising depth to which themes are explored makes for a memorable and endearing experience in Grand Theft Auto VI, which largely lives up to its sky-high expectations by inverting the series’s reputation for destruction.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By this point I'm probably safe in assuming that you all know EA are shutting down BioWare, and that Mass Effect 5 has been cancelled in turn. You may have also seen that an internal trailer for Mass Effect 5, or Universe as it was seemingly going to be called, was leaked not long after the news broke, and that Sam Hulick, one of the composers on the original trilogy of games, shared he was going to offer up his re-scored version of the trailer. Well, it's N7 Day, as rough as that will be for many of the developers on the game, but Hulick has stood by his word, and shared an oral glimpse at what the world of Mass Effect Universe could have sounded like.

It has been revealed that you can check out this fresh version of the trailer below, perhaps pop it on while you have a read of the rest of this post, as Hulick did also write in a Patreon blog about his experience with the series. "As part of my own closure, and as a love letter to the fans, I really wanted to re-score the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer in time for N7 Day this year," he wrote. "BioWare edited a killer track called “Quartz” by French 79 to fit their trailer, which I think hinted at a slight directional shift in the score. Using that as inspiration, along with the musical tone from my work on the first three Mass Effect games, I hit the studio and got to work.".

As it turns out, BioWare had actually reached out to Hulick asking him to potentially do some work for the project. "This year, BioWare emailed me asking if I was interested in working with them on an internal demo, and they stated they were 'hoping to get some music written that would feel like Mass [Effect], supporting our new direction.' Of course, I said yes!" This doesn't mean he wouldn't have composed the actual game, as a composer hadn't been officially selected, but Hulick said he was "more than happy to collaborate on the new game’s musical direction and help make their internal demo sound as good as it could.".

It has been revealed that hulick also spoke of some of the ideas he had for the direction Mass Effect Universe's soundtrack could take, noting how he "thought it would’ve been incredible to bring more songs with lyrics into the game," considering how many people loved the first game's end-credits song. "This would’ve been a great way to highlight more emotional moments in the narrative. Artists at the top of my collaboration list included Gunship, NINA, and The Midnight, all of whom have a moody, cinematic synthwave vibe that would’ve meshed well with the score in my head. And I’m pretty sure the Gunship guys are gamers, and if they’re Mass Effect fans, that would’ve been the icing on the cake!".

Of course, with the studio now closing, this never got to go very far, the news hitting Hulick "particularly hard, as the Mass Effect trilogy is a core part of my origin story as a composer." For the composer, ultimately "this trailer is my way of saying goodbye… at least for now." This continues to be a horrendously sad moment in the industry! As always, solidarity with the team at BioWare.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Phasmophobia community has raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

In a recent development, developer Kinetic Games declared the final figure for this year's Ghost Hunts for Hearts event on 6th November. The charity drive ran from 26th October to 2nd November, and more than 500 streamers signed up to take part. That's the biggest turnout yet for a creator fundraiser run by Heart Liive, the American Heart Association's streaming initiative.

Last year's event raised a little over $100,000.

Recent findings suggest that streamers who fundraised could hand out an event-exclusive Advocate ID Card and Badge to their viewers as a Twitch Drop. Kinetic set a target of $200,000 at the start of the week, and once players sailed past it, an animated version of the card and badge set unlocked for all.

"The Phasmophobia community never fails to amaze us, and this year they've outdone themselves," mentioned Tom Dent, lead social media and player experience manager at Kinetic Games. "Thank you to every streamer, viewer and player who took part.".

Phasmophobia introduced in Early Access in September 2020, and sends teams of up to four players into haunted locations to gather evidence of what's lurking there.

Recent findings suggest that the studio also released a publishing arm, Kinetic Publishing, earlier this year. Its first game, the starship job simulator Contact Protocol, is due out in spring 2027.

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio remarked it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Update. The studio ended up apologising to players for problems with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next substantial game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

Recent findings suggest that these figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

According to recent reports, assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a significant launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ocarina of Time's notoriously tricky Master Quest mode could be making a comeback in the fresh remake.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ocarina of Time's notoriously tricky Master Quest mode could be making a comeback in the fresh remake.

Dataminer MrCheeze shared a list of strings from the remake's files on Bluesky, several of which tie the tag "MQ" to dungeons like Dodongo's Cavern.

In a follow-up, as spotted by TheGamer, they pointed to further entries, including "HasMQ", "IsMQModeExist", "NewGameMQ", and "ReleaseMQ".

Fellow dataminer OatmealDome added on Twitter/X that the mode will be unlocked by owning DLC, rather than arriving in an enhancement, though "the data is incomplete". "I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly)," they noted.

If you've not played it, Master Quest is a remixed version of Ocarina of Time with rearranged dungeons and tougher puzzles. It first appeared as a bonus disc on GameCube, then came back in 2011's Ocarina of Time 3D, which unlocked it after you finished the main game. That version also mirrored the whole world, which matches what OatmealDome has found, and had enemies deal double damage.

[Ocarina of Time] #ootspoilersThere is data in the game files for Master Quest. It will be unlocked by *owning DLC* - it is not just an enhancement.The data is incomplete, but I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly).

As with any datamine, there's no guarantee it'll ever see the light of day. Nintendo hasn't declared any DLC for the remake, and it's not clear whether Master Quest would be free, like it was on 3DS, or paid.

According to recent reports, the Ocarina of Time remake launched on Switch 2 on 5th November. Donlan called the newly introduced version an "astonishing remake" in his five-star Eurogamer Ocarina of Time review.

Industry observers note that I know what you want. The humble city builder isn't enough for you any more, is it? You need a cities builder, you can't just stop at one, but you don't want to build up an entirely different city on a latest save file. If it were up to you, they'd all be on the same map, a motorway's worth of a drive away from each other. If we're talking contemporary cities, I can't help you, but if you can settle for numerous medieval towns across an entire county, then County of Fortune should do just fine.

It has been revealed that county of Fortune just landed in early access a couple of days ago, and as mentioned (and as the name suggests), you're building up an entire county! "You place whole settlements across the county and lay each one out on a medieval grid. Each one grows, specializes, and knits into a living region where rivers and resources decide what thrives," the game's Steam page explains. "As the county matures, a second game begins. Named mayors run each settlement. Rival noble houses weave politics across the region. And migrating cultures bless some villages, while complicating others.".

To start with, it's up to you where you want to place each of your settlements, deciding how they individually function as you do. The towns are then partially procedurally generated as they get built up, slowly connecting to other nearby towns. "The scale is the point. You are not zooming into a single town - you are zooming out to see a whole county come to life." A big part of the strategy comes down to how you navigate the map; finding resource deposits, picking appropriate terrain profiles, utilising rivers efficiently, finding a good climate, setting good trade routes, it's all about working with the land you've got.

Each settlement will produce different things depending on the materials available to them in close proximity, meaning each one has a unique function. You've got different types of characters to consider too: mayors, noble houses and cultures, all intersecting with different elements of how a town functions. Seems like a unique approach to city building! And as mentioned, it's out in early access; you can pick it up on Steam here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era.
  • In a recent development, the two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17.
  • Sources indicate that the Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis confirmed The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

In a recent development, the two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

Sources indicate that the Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Sources indicate that created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature rolls out, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It has been revealed that it is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

It has been revealed that in order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In a recent development, in the blog post announcing the latest features, Maxis stated that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

In a recent development, you can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

According to recent reports, since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Sources indicate that alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

According to recent reports, sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

It has been revealed that the last 30 minutes have been, quite frankly, massive for the world of video games. Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews dropped, and it's officially the highest-rated game ever released. The review embargo coincided with the game's release in Latest Zealand, as midnight struck in that territory. Players are now starting to get their hands on the game.

Sources indicate that while some are opting to take "sneaky flights," changing the time on their consoles to gain access to it early, others have just opted to passively view things. Within 30 minutes, the game has broken the Twitch record for the most-viewed single-player game of all time, and it's undoubtedly about to break the most-viewed game record imminently.

Before today, according to Guinness World Records, the most-viewed single-player game of all time on Twitch peaked at 1,280,000. That was Hogwarts Legacy, back in 2023. 30 minutes after launch, Grand Theft Auto 6 obliterated that record.

In a recent development, as of right now, there are over 2.5 million viewers in the GTA 6 category on Twitch, each one itching to get an early view of what the game contains. Streamer Alanzoka has 227,000 viewers alone, and others like xQc and TheBurntPeanut have 99,000 and 48,000, respectively.

Recent findings suggest that the multiplayer record looks set to tumble shortly. According to TwitchTracker, League of Legends holds the record for the most concurrent viewers for a multiplayer game, peaking at 3,111,023 back in November 2022. Grand Theft Auto 6 is 80 percent of the way there, and half of the United States, Twitch's biggest audience, is still asleep. Valorant holds the record for most viewing hours in a single day at 34 million, but there's almost no chance it'll hold on, with GTA likely to smash it today.

It has been revealed that prior to release, the game was already breaking records, becoming the most preordered game in history, with at least 10 million preorders. That was nine days before release, so that almost certainly doubled. If you're planning to play at midnight in your local time, just make sure you follow PlayStation's latest piece of mandatory advice.

  • Industry observers note that "Look, Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Call of Duty is an inherently conservative series. You know what you're getting: guns, explosions, cinematic flourishes inspired by action movies, and probably some jingoism. And that's largely what the annual series' adherents seem to want. But it could be so much more.

Sources indicate that taylor Kurosaki, writer and co-director for Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, tells us he still thinks it has broad potential. That's why Infinite Warfare was set in the future—though, at the time, the team didn't realise it would end up being the third futuristic CoD, following Advanced Warfare and Black Ops 3.

Industry observers note that "Look, Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right? It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty.".

According to recent reports, I would love for that to be true. Call of Duty: The American Revolutionary War, Call of Duty: The Hundred Years War, Call of Duty: Napoleon. A military romp that isn't set between 1941 and 2065. After 23 years, it would be nice to see it spread out a bit.

Recent findings suggest that but massive swings are not in CoD's nature. Or rather, Activision isn't particularly interested in rocking the money boat. A medieval CoD isn't the only massive detour the series almost took. Before it was forced to salvage Infinity Ward's Modern Warfare 3, Sledgehammer was working on a third-person horror game set in Vietnam, called Call of Duty: Fog of War.

"We wanted to make a scary version of Vietnam," Sledgehammer co-founder Glen Schofield told us last year. "And not just scary, we wanted intense battles that were personal, but stuff you've never seen before. We were making it, and we were really psyched about having you go through tunnels, and everything is scary because there's not much light down there. Sometimes you're shooting in the dark.".

In a recent development, when Vince Zampella and Jason West left Infinity Ward amid a legal dispute, Activision told Sledgehammer to drop their project and pivot to Modern Warfare 3. It was never allowed to return to Fog of War.
