📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that years ago, I had this dream where I was parkouring through a greatly sunken version of Venice, no doubt sourced from the many hours I put into Assassin's Creed 2 as a teen who should have been studying for their GCSEs a lot more than they were. It's stuck with me after all this time mostly because of how much I wanted to capture that feeling again somehow, as the real Assassin's Creed didn't quite cut it. And lo and behold, there I was today browsing Bluesky when I came across Boars in Rome, a Mirror's Edge and Counter Strike Surf inspired parkour platformer set in a dystopian version of Rome.

Recent findings suggest that truthfully, witnessing the clip I've shared below was baffling to me. "This is what I dreamt of!" More or less, anyway, for the setting isn't quite the same; "You have been selected to start a new life off planet. Earth has been abandoned," explains the game's Steam page. "Machines keep working and nature claims what remains. Find out what happened while you were frozen in time by exploring the remnants of Rome where historical monuments mix with futurist megastructures.".

Mirrors Edge x Counter Strike Surf where you parkour on anything! Be smooth n stylish in dystopian Rome. Or just jump around and explore, whatever works for you. It's called Boars in Rome! #PitchYaGame[image or embed].

Industry observers note that not all of it matches that dream of mine, some of it leans much more into brutalism than the typical, much older architecture you'd expect of Rome, but it's there nonetheless. In motion, Boars in Rome feels quite oneiric too. There is so much more control over the game's avatar than what my real body is capable of, or wants to do. You can run, jump, slide and wallrun, positioning it quite closely to VHOLUME mechanically. Where it differs is in its additives, movement tech like being able to swing on lampposts or vault over low down obstacles.

VHOLUME is more of a game about providing you with a simple toolkit and leaving you to push it to its maximum. Boars in Roam is a touch more expressive, and I'd dare to even call it an immersive sim. The levels you can romp around are linear, you have an end point to reach, only the journey is up to you. It certainly feels appropriate to put it in the im sim camp given that, at least the game's first level, calls to mind Viktor Antonov's work on Dishonored (and Half-Life 2, too, honestly).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has officially been out in the wild for a good few weeks now, and that's given fans plenty of time to uncover get-rich-quick exploits – including one that's made a good few players especially wealthy… much to the community's dismay.

According to recent reports, dungeons have been an especially hot topic in the community since the MMO left Beta earlier this month, with fan feedback on them leading to a 50% XP boost and further changes as recently as yesterday. The whole experience controversy isn't the only reason dungeons – specifically the Blackmaw Hold – have been in the limelight, though. An exploit that grants folks hundreds of thousands of gold is another.

Recent findings suggest that blizzard did nerf the exploit this week, which let players burst through enemies for wildly expensive drops in the dungeon over and over again; however, its effects on the economy of WoW: Forever are, unsurprisingly, lasting. So much so, in fact, that those innocent of the exploit's shady dealings are calling for Blizzard to enact a heavier hand. Over on its official forums, for example, one fan writes, "Remove the gold and ban them." They continue: "Remove the gold or I and many others will just quit. This is worse than the bots at this point." Comments see fellow players agreeing with the poster, with the top response reading, "100% the gold needs to be removed and bans need to be handed out." It's not an isolated conversation, either. Threads on Reddit see fans sharing in on the sentiment, with one in particular drawing attention to Blizzard axing the "100+ gold per hour farm.".

It has been revealed that replies align well with those on the World of Warcraft forums. "Remove all gold and hand out at minimum a month ban," one exclaims. "Make them miss raid introduces or straight up permaban them." They're not the only person to call for a permanent ban here: "If they don't revert gold earned, the economy is already shot with an exploit mafia controlling the market. Remove all gold and ban one month or permaban.".

It might seem like a drastic response, but this isn't the first time WoW: Forever fans have had to grapple with gold-related cheating. Back during the beta, Blizzard actually nabbed a good $200 worth of gold off a streamer who was, uh, pretty public with it (spoiler alert: they likely got it via real-money trading, which is strictly forbidden). Prior to that, the studio had stated that its fresh MMO's economy is "something we're taking very seriously" as well.

According to recent reports, so, will we see Blizzard crack down more strongly and dish out some bans to players abusing patched exploits like the Blackmaw Hold one in question here? Only time can tell, I suppose, but I'd argue it'll already have a negative effect on the game's economy by then, sadly.

Blizzard knows World of Warcraft: Forever has a gold problem – but that doesn't mean a feature everyone used to grind it in the OG MMO is coming back.

And while it's not uncommon for Call of Duty titles to make some of their modes available for free for a limited time, the timing of this DMZ taster is notable.

DMZ released days before Modern Warfare 4's 23rd October release date, meaning this first trial has arrived just two weeks after the game's full launch. By comparison, Black Ops 7's Endgame mode had its first free trial months after launch, in the game's third season. That mentioned, Endgame continued to be freely available until Season 6.

Sources indicate that the DMZ trial also coincides with the launch of Modern Warfare 4's iteration of free-to-play Call of Duty battle royale mode Warzone, and Season 1. Indeed, both DMZ and the latest Warzone take place on the same Hajin map, so even if you don't decide to buy the full game to continue playing DMZ, some of that map knowledge will certainly transfer to Warzone.

Recent findings suggest that the DMZ trial does not appear to have any limits, meaning you can climb the ranks, access Story Missions - the only way to play PvE, with caveats - and complete Orders to your heart's content. That includes X01, the new endgame dungeon-like area available to experienced and fully-equipped players.

DMZ players who've been asking Infinity Ward to offer a PvE-only playlist of the PvPvE mode will certainly be happy with the influx of newly introduced players, as they could potentially amplify their calls for a PvP-free playlist.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • We awarded it a score of 7/10 in our review.
  • Industry observers note that but if you take a look on Metacritic, you'd think Nintendo just put out its worst game in years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is out now, bringing 4K visuals to the 2023 title along with the new Dandori Academy mode and some neat little extras like voice commands.

We awarded it a score of 7/10 in our review. It's still good – hell, the main Pikmin 4 campaign is possibly the best of the bunch – yet we can't deny our disappointment at the lack of mouse controls and 60fps performance.

Industry observers note that but if you take a look on Metacritic, you'd think Nintendo just put out its worst game in years. Although the metascore is sitting at a commendable 83, the game's user score is much, much lower at 2.3. This essentially means its average is 'Generally Unfavourable'. Yeesh.

Recent findings suggest that most folks just seem disgruntled at the notion that Nintendo is charging for what they perceive to be a very minor upgrade over the original. It's true that a lot of games over the years have received free updates for newer hardware, but Nintendo has opted to charge £7.99 / $9.99 / €9.99.

Sources indicate that "This switch 2 edition is essentially worthless. At worst it's a spit in the face of series fans. $20 AUD for a bunch of recycled content and 4k visuals. They couldn't even be bothered to implement 60fps even though the system could definitely handle it. Such a lazy update, and yet they have the gall to charge $20 AUD.".

Meanwhile, another user provided a slightly more measured assessment, stating:.

"The Dandori Academy has reused content, half of the maps so far are taken directly from the base game and the other half share the same exact layout. Plus the latest card on the title screen looks like an ad, ruins the nice scenery, fortunately it can be hidden.

In a recent development, "The main game has also suffered, now somehow having longer loading times than it did on the original Switch. All other Switch 2 editions have made them shorter, so this is really weird. It's not a small difference either, some have literally doubled.".

The comment about the load times is particularly interesting.

Industry observers note that this has been highlighted elsewhere, with YouTuber 'Press A!' posting an analysis titled 'Pikmin 4's DLC is a disaster...' (flexing that signature YouTube nuance right there) in which he compares the load times of the Switch 2 Edition with the original. When exiting out of a cave, the original would take around 6 seconds or so to load the main environment, however the same moment took over 30 seconds in the Switch 2 version.

A few people have mentioned the load times being quite long, so we tested it out ourselves. While loading into a cave takes about 6 seconds, loading out took around 14-15 seconds. Not the 30+ that others are citing, then, but probably long enough to raise an eyebrow or two.

Pikmin 4's user score on Switch 2 is a startling contrast to that of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Despite some concerns here and there regarding the game's overall difficulty and approachability compared to the original, Ocarina of Time commands the highest user score of all time at 9.6.

We'll be curious to see whether Nintendo takes any steps to improve the load times in Pikmin 4, but for what you actually get with the new content and visual enhancements on Switch 2, we'd say the upgrade price is probably appropriate. It'll tide us over until Pikmin 5, at least.

Please note voting will score the game in your games collection.

It has been revealed that what are your thoughts on Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition so far? Do you think the complaints are valid, or have they taken it a bit too far? Let us know with a comment.

How Wuthering Waves Brings Its Evolving World to Life Through Character Design, Music and Storytelling

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article was produced in collaboration with our sponsor, Kuro Games.
  • Solaris-3 is a world still recovering from the Lament, a cataclysm that reshaped its land and left Tacet Discords roaming the ruins.
  • It has been revealed that since launch, that world has grown far beyond its starting point in Huanglong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article was produced in collaboration with our sponsor, Kuro Games.

Solaris-3 is a world still recovering from the Lament, a cataclysm that reshaped its land and left Tacet Discords roaming the ruins. Players enter it as the Rover, a wanderer with no memory, and rebuild their understanding of the world one region at a time.

It has been revealed that since launch, that world has grown far beyond its starting point in Huanglong. Rinascita, Lahai-Roi and now the Simulacrum Nexus of Mengzhou in Version 3.7 have each added new cultures, new Resonators and new mysteries to uncover. Version 3.8 sets the stage for the next major chapter, paving the way for Version 4.0 and the arrival of the New Federation.

It has been revealed that but Wuthering Waves does more than add newly introduced places and faces. It gives every addition meaning through three connected creative pillars: character design, music and storytelling. Together, they turn new content into something players feel, not just something they unlock.

According to recent reports, in Wuthering Waves, a Resonator's outfit is a passport. Costume, color, silhouette and animation tell you where a character comes from and what role they play, often before they say a word.

The clearest example is Rinascita, whose cast looks like it belongs to a single, coherent culture while each member stays distinct:.

The same idea carries across Solaris-3:.

Sources indicate that if the costume introduces a character, animation brings them to life. Jinhsi, the Magistrate of Jinzhou, moves with poised, ceremonial grace that suits a leader. The Shorekeeper's calm, drifting motions reflect her role as a quiet guardian of the Black Shores. Even an Intro Skill becomes a small character beat.

Each new region gives Kuro Games a new artistic direction to explore, from Huanglong's flowing robes to Rinascita's carnival and gladiator styles, and on to the tribal and futuristic looks of Lahai-Roi. The cast grows more varied with every revision, yet still reads as one world.

It has been revealed that if character design tells you who belongs where, music tells you how it feels to be there. The soundtrack's strength comes down to three ideas: genre fusion, musical world building and lyrics that tell stories.

Wuthering Waves rarely sticks to a single genre. A track might set its mood with synthesizers and programmed drums, then hand the melody to strings, piano or electric guitar. Cartethyia's "With Glory I Shall Fall" blends orchestral instruments with synth bass and electric guitar: the orchestra brings grandeur, while the guitar and bass add urgency and a modern edge. The mix is deliberate, matching a world where ancient tradition and advanced technology sit side by side.

The soundtrack changes its musical vocabulary as you travel. The music of Huanglong is anchored by sweeping melodies and traditional instrumental timbres, creating a tranquil yet deeply narrative atmosphere. Rinascita’s soundtrack is brighter and more vibrant, blending romanticism with dramatic tension—echoing the seaport city-state’s rich artistic heritage. Meanwhile, Lahai-Roi leans toward a modern pop aesthetic, complementing its science-fiction, academic setting. You can sense a region's identity through its music before you know its history.

Vocal tracks are part of the storytelling, not decoration. Phrolova's theme, "Reveries in the Crimson Beyond", speaks to a dream as if asking it for comfort and tech giant, reflecting her longing to stay inside an imagined world and hold on to moments she has lost. Players who know her story hear the lyrics differently, and the song in turn deepens their understanding of her.

The emotional power of Wuthering Waves’ music does not end when players leave the game. Through To the New World, the game’s first global concert tour, its music travelled from the virtual world into reality, visiting six cities—Shanghai, Tokyo, Seoul, Taipei, Singapore and Los Angeles—and attracting nearly 50,000 attendees worldwide. Blending orchestral performances, live vocals, band arrangements and immersive stage productions, the concert brought familiar melodies and character themes to life in new ways. It also rekindled memories of pivotal story moments and beloved characters, giving players the chance to relive those emotions together and experience a second emotional resonance with the game.

Recent findings suggest that that commitment has also earned industry recognition. After “Against the Tide” won the 2025 HMMA for Song – Video Game (Console & PC), Wuthering Waves received three more nominations in 2026—across original song, mobile-game music and live concert performance. These honors reflect how the game treats music not merely as accompaniment, but as the emotional heartbeat of its characters and world.

The world of Wuthering Waves feels alive because its story never stops moving. Characters change, conflicts shift, and places carry the marks of what happened there.

The Rover's search for lost memories is the thread that runs through every region. Each Main Quest chapter pulls the Rover deeper into the mysteries of the Lament and the forces shaping Solaris-3, giving players a reason to keep moving forward.

The larger plot matters because the people in it do. Character-related quests explore what drives each Resonator: their loyalties, their losses and the choices they struggle with. When a Resonator you know steps into a Main Quest, the stakes feel personal.

According to recent reports, each region introduces its own culture, politics and conflicts. Huanglong wrestles with duty and protection, Rinascita with faith and tradition, and Lahai-Roi with knowledge and the future. Version 3.7 brought the Xuanfang arc to its finale in the Simulacrum Nexus of Mengzhou.

Recent findings suggest that not every story is told in dialogue. Ruined cities, overgrown battlefields and quiet landmarks hint at the history behind them, rewarding players who explore and look closely.

Every major update adds a latest chapter of history, a new set of characters and a new storyline. Instead of a fixed world, Solaris-3 is one that keeps changing alongside the people who live in it.

Wuthering Waves is at its best when design, music and story work as one, and nearly every Resonator in the cast is built this way. Here are three examples of how it works.

It has been revealed that design. Cartethyia’s dual-form design brings her past and present together. Her Cartethyia form reflects the free wandering knight she has become, while Fleurdelys recalls the Blessed Maiden, vessel of Divinity and Queen of Gale and Tide she once was. Fate bestowed upon her the title of the Blessed Maiden, but it was her own choices that gave the title its true meaning.

Recent findings suggest that music. Her theme, "With Glory I Shall Fall", mirrors that duality. Orchestral grandeur speaks to the legend of the Blessed Maiden, while electric guitar and synth bass bring the force of the warrior who fights for Rinascita.

Sources indicate that story. Her story gives both of them meaning. Once you learn how the title of Blessed Maiden came to rest on her shoulders, her two forms and her theme stop being separate details and become one character.

None of the three would land as hard alone. Together, they make Cartethyia unforgettable.

In a recent development, design. One of Aemeath's most distinctive design features is the transformation between her human and mech forms. The mech is a transformation form born from her past as an Exostrider Synchronist, as well as an extension of her own abilities. Elements of Fleet Snowfluff's design are also incorporated into the mech, making it both a reflection of her childhood admiration for heroes and an essential means through which she fights and protects others. The seamless transitions between her two forms, along with their cooperative combat, further reinforce the connection between them.

Music. As the digital songstress known as Fleet Snowfluff, music plays an integral role in Aemeath's characterization. In her character teaser, Memories of Fleet Snowfluff, we see her wholeheartedly practicing her songs. Her voice fits perfectly with Lahai-Roi's contemporary pop-inspired musical style. More notably, the development team uses forward and reversed versions of the same melody to represent different timelines, connecting Aemeath's childhood and adult selves through a shared musical motif. As the truth behind her story gradually unfolds, players come to realize that these melodies had been quietly foreshadowing the emotional revelations all along.

According to recent reports, story. If her design and music bring Aemeath's character to life, then the Version 3.1 Main Quest reveals the reasons behind these creative choices. She was once an Exostrider Synchronist at Startorch Academy, and an ordinary girl with dreams of her own. However, after resonating with the Exostrider and pushing herself into Overclock, she lost her physical body and became a digital ghost. Her encounters with Rover also form a causal loop centered on connection, memory, and protection.

Design. Hsin is the Sentinel of Mengzhou and the first playable Sentinel. In combat she splits into fox forms, a striking image for a guardian who is more than she first appears.

It has been revealed that music. Her theme, "Ode to Hsin and Moon", is a vocal song composed by Jin Dazhou and sung by Jaime Arin. It comes in two versions, "Endless Yearning" and "Whither Away?", and the titles alone give her two moods: a longing that never fades, and a question of where her path will lead.

Recent findings suggest that story. Version 3.7 closes the Xuanfang arc around her. Her storyline completes the logical loop of her audiovisual design: it unveils why her character design highlights power while her music reflects an inner uncertainty, bringing both sides into unity through her story.

Sources indicate that three regions, three very different Resonators, yet in each one design, music and story point the same way. That harmony is what makes the world of Wuthering Waves feel alive.

In a recent development, wuthering Waves keeps growing, but size is not what makes Solaris-3 memorable. What sets it apart is how each upcoming region and Resonator arrives fully realized: dressed in a look that belongs to their culture, carried by music that gives them an emotional voice, and woven into a story that connects them to everything around them.

Through Version 3.7, that approach has taken players from the halls of Jinzhou to the carnival streets of Rinascita, the frontiers of Lahai-Roi and the heart of Xuanfang. With Version 3.8 now live, Rovers will find their paths crossing more and more with the Upcoming Federation. A new story is about to set off from here. Wherever the Rover heads next, one thing seems certain: the next chapter of Solaris-3 will be worth seeing, hearing and feeling.

GTA 6 is due to release on the 19th November on PS5, and Xbox Series X/S, and ahead of the highly-anticipated launch of Rockstar's latest sandbox adventure, people just can't get enough information about the game. To that end, overnight, we saw our latest leak: the game will have 55 Trophies/Achievements.

In a now-deleted tweet from (in)famous Rockstar dataminer, TexFunz2 - re-posted by the Twitter account iGrandTheftAuto - it appears the game will have 55 individual rewards for completing certain tasks and missions. At the time of writing, we don't know specifically what these challenges are, but it seems none of them will be attached to the online version of the game; the base game rolls out without GTA Online, and so we can safely assume that all these rewards will be for the single-player only content. GTA Online will drop sometime in 2027, according to Twitch's CEO.

Sources indicate that if you've been paying attention to previous Rockstar titles, you'll know that Grand Theft Auto 5 launched with 51 Achievements/Trophies - again, all single-player - and Red Dead Redemption 2 launched with 52. So the latest game has more than either game got at launch - and I can tell you from experience, getting Platinum in either title was a very time-consuming experience. Expect the same to be true here, too.

Sources indicate that it's worth highlighting that GTA 5 did, eventually, get more Achievements and Trophies: the GTA Online content upped the complete total to 78, adding 27 latest challenges to complete. I would expect GTA 6 to do the same… whenever the PC version of GTA comes out, or GTA Online lands in the new game (it's possible both could happen at the same time).

In a recent development, recently, we heard why a former Rockstar Games tech director thinks GTA 6 could be coming to PC sooner than you'd expect (mostly thanks to AI clones), when we can expect the pre-load of the game (10th November), and how big the final game install is expected to be (210GB). The final game is expected to be so big and dense with detail that no single Rockstar employee has seen the entire game, meaning there are plenty of easter eggs and ridiculous things to discover.

Final Fantasy 14's ongoing pursuit in making its 500-hour story less daunting almost manifested into something in August, but Yoshi-P decided to postpone it

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that I love Final Fantasy 14.
  • We know, at the very least, that director and producer Naoki Yoshida has been thinking about ways to make that barrier to entry a little less frightening—he mentioned as much during Final Fantasy 14's Berlin Fan Festival—but according to a recent Letter from the Producer, it turns out we could've actually had something as recently as August.
  • "The idea of letting players freely choose a starting point for their adventure has been discussed, with the goal being to offer players a range of choices, rather than prescribe their experience according to my philosophy," Yoshida wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I love Final Fantasy 14. I can also recognise that for anyone trying to start the game in the substantial 2026, it's incredibly daunting. Being faced with A Realm Reborn and five entire expansions' worth of story is a lot, and the question of how to funnel newly introduced players into Eorzea in a more approachable manner while still respecting the MMO's heavily narrative-driven vibe has been an ongoing debate for the last several years.

We know, at the very least, that director and producer Naoki Yoshida has been thinking about ways to make that barrier to entry a little less frightening—he mentioned as much during Final Fantasy 14's Berlin Fan Festival—but according to a recent Letter from the Producer, it turns out we could've actually had something as recently as August.

"The idea of letting players freely choose a starting point for their adventure has been discussed, with the goal being to offer players a range of choices, rather than prescribe their experience according to my philosophy," Yoshida wrote.

Recent findings suggest that in case you're not familiar with Yoshida's whole stance on this, he's long been staunchly protective of Final Fantasy 14's narrative integrity. Story skips are locked to the cash shop and, up until now, never included the current expansion. He's repeatedly expressed the fact that he's not too keen on letting people jump in wherever they feel, since it kinda mucks up the decade-plus worldbuilding and character relationships the game has built.

But, like many things he's been opposed to introducing in the game like unlocked glamour, he's letting up for the sake of allowing players more agency in how they engage with the game.

Anyway, back to letting people tackle its immense story a little easier. "With New Game+ working smoothly, this approach could work," Yoshida surmised. "In fact, we'd been laying groundwork to make this a possibility in conjunction with the release of the Nintendo Switch 2 version, but ultimately decided to postpone this initiative.".

Sources indicate that I do wonder specifically what made them stop—whether there was a hiccup somewhere, or whether Yoshida simply decided now wasn't the right time. He also expresses concern about a mismatch in player skill between those who jump ahead and those who've been around the block. "Even if you could start adventuring from a point of your choosing, the time and effort required to master a job remain a constant," he wrote. "We also need to avoid situations where both newly introduced and veteran players are left confused when matched together.".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

I don't want to be the one to tell Yoshi-P that the mismatch is still there even among players who've been around a long time, but I've seen an awful lot of omni-level characters who can't even do their basic rotation. So there's that.

Sources indicate that "However, with all these considerations in mind, we've held meetings to discuss system and tutorial improvements, and have set ourselves a significant goal for the future. Although we'll need more time to realise this goal, I think giving players more freedom in their adventures will ultimately prove a positive change.".

Honestly? I think even without story skips, tutorialisation and job mastery need to be better woven into the fabric of the game. Its low-level Hall of the Novice misses crucial info and includes odd holdovers from the days of things like the TP resource and much tougher aggro management—there's no emphasis on the importance of healers dealing damage, and tanks are told to only use their AOE for aggro generation before switching to single target.

It's all well and good trying to help players understand their role, but not when the information is outdated and fails to include key responsibilities. The tactical training exercises introduced early in Dawntrail are much better, and show how helpful such tutorials can be when they're properly updated and in line with over a decade's worth of in-game culture and community expectations.

It has been revealed that mollie spent her early childhood deeply invested in games like Killer Instinct, Toontown and Audition Online, which continue to form the pillars of her personality today. She joined PC Gamer in 2020 as a news writer and now lends her expertise to write a wealth of features, guides and reviews with a dash of chaos. She can often be found causing mischief in Final Fantasy 14, using those experiences to write neat things about her favourite MMO. When she's not staring at her bunny girl she can be found sweating out rhythm games, pretending to be good at fighting games or spending far too much money at her local arcade.

Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the substantial Diablo 4 Developer Revision has indeed delivered the goods.
  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
  • Sources indicate that season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the substantial Diablo 4 Developer Revision has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Sources indicate that season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

It has been revealed that when you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the fresh Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

It has been revealed that if you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a upcoming event that rewards you for killing enemies promptly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

It has been revealed that anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

It has been revealed that there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a newly introduced item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the upcoming class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

According to recent reports, season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever has received a massive buff to the XP drop-rates of dungeon mobs (enemies), which should make running these instances multiple times feel more rewarding - and may revive an older levelling strategy.
  • Recent findings suggest that this buff is a 50 percent increase in experience from all mobs killed inside all dungeons.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever developers have spoken in the past about the decision to deliberately bring down dungeon mob XP to disincentivise power-levelling in dungeons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has received a massive buff to the XP drop-rates of dungeon mobs (enemies), which should make running these instances multiple times feel more rewarding - and may revive an older levelling strategy.

Recent findings suggest that this buff is a 50 percent increase in experience from all mobs killed inside all dungeons. As detailed in this World of Warcraft forum post, community manager Kaivax wrote that this change has been made "so it feels better to go back in for more runs". They don't outright say this is in response to community feedback, but the subject has been a hot topic since the beta.

World of Warcraft: Forever developers have spoken in the past about the decision to deliberately bring down dungeon mob XP to disincentivise power-levelling in dungeons. The idea was that by doing this, people would be encouraged to actually go out into the world and explore it, rather than hopping from instance to instance until they reached max level.

In a recent development, sadly, a side effect of this change is that doing a dungeon more than once could feel unrewarding. Playing it once is great, as you get to complete lots of quests that reward guaranteed items and XP. However, if you go back again, you don't get these, so your only source of progression comes from a heavily decreased XP rate.

Some quests exacerbate this matter. Dungeons like Wailing Caverns and especially Blackfathom Deeps have a quest that can't really be completed in one run due to a reliance on drop rates for items you need, and having to fight for drops with the rest of your dungeon party. Having to go back to complete this used to suck, and now it sucks less!

So does this mean farming dungeons to power-level is back? Maybe, but it still won't be nearly as efficient as it was in older versions of Classic WoW. The current mob XP rates, after this buff, will still only be 36 percent of the original Classic rate - a third. Given how fast you can level by doing quests out in the world, it seems dungeon farming isn't due for a comeback just yet.

It has been revealed that after an especially smooth launch, World of Warcraft: Forever has become the biggest launch in the series' history, beating out Wrath of the Lich King, Cataclysm, and all the other past expansion launches. The developers have been quick to hotfix things on the fly, including a change that left PvP battlegrounds heavily advantaged for the Horde.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, while its remastered upgrade might have broken cover in late September, The Witcher 3's extra expansion isn't set to join it until next year.
  • According to recent reports, so far, only the opening chapter of the mod - Annals of the Duchy - has been released.
  • Recent findings suggest that the mod's creator, Jontej, has previously put together a couple of other custom Witcher 3 quests.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, while its remastered upgrade might have broken cover in late September, The Witcher 3's extra expansion isn't set to join it until next year. With 2027 still a month and a bit away, a modder's taken it upon themselves to add a few more adventures to Geralt's time in Toussaint, Blood and Wine's gorgeous French-ish duchy, before the bloke from the river heads off to Letten for Songs of the Past.

According to recent reports, so far, only the opening chapter of the mod - Annals of the Duchy - has been released. It adds in a newly introduced quest about Geralt, with help from either Yen or Triss if either have made the trip out to Toussaint as part of your playthrough, getting into a scrape thanks to a halfling who seems to promise Gerry the chance to juice up his vineyard's vines.

Recent findings suggest that the mod's creator, Jontej, has previously put together a couple of other custom Witcher 3 quests. While they do look to have used AI voices in English versions of those mods, for Annals of the Duchy they've enlisted a cast of human actors for both Enlish and Polish versions.

Jontej has plans to expand this new questline going forwards, having cited specific "plans for an extra storyline involving Syanna", whom you might remember from Blood and Wine's main quest. Given that - spoilers ahead - the mod relies on you having gotten the Blood and Wine ending which sees both Anna Henrietta and Syanna survive, as well as having paid to renovate the gardens of Geralt's vineyard. They add that, when it comes to their additions, the "timeline fits quite well [with] the upcoming official Songs of the Past Expansion, which has been confirmed to take place after the events of the main game/Blood and Wine".

As much as I've argued that, as of right now, I struggle to see how Songs of the Past will manage to outdo Blood and Wine as a satisfying end to Geralt's tale in the Witcher game trilogy, I am intrigued by the idea of a few more modded adventures showing Gerry adjusting to the semi-retired life. After all, Toussaint's got to have a few more dungeons tucked away that're worth temporarily dusting off the White Wolf's twin swords for.

To kick off Annals of the Duchy, you'll need to trigger its first quest by taking a stroll from the Corvo Bianco manor house down to its gardens between 11am and 1pm. It's worth noting that any other mod which messes with Yen, Triss or companions in general has a chance to muck things up as far as Jontej's creation goes.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Between sending mob bosses to swim with the fish and bowling with his cousin in GTA 4, Niko Bellic visits an internet café to chat with women online.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto games are time capsules, and I'm not just talking about the anachronistic entries like Vice City that unravel the glitz and seedy glamour of '80s Miami movies.

Between sending mob bosses to swim with the fish and bowling with his cousin in GTA 4, Niko Bellic visits an internet café to chat with women online. The entire interface is a relic of early naughties forums and crude online shopping, something that GTA 5 would iterate on and bring to mobile. Part of making the game world feel real meant tackling the online world, and Rockstar understood that—right down to emailing, an infamous LCPD sting operation, and in-game news sites. GTA 6, however, is bucking that trend, getting rid of the internet entirely for something much more 2026.

Recent findings suggest that in an interview with Kotaku ahead of the game's launch, Rockstar explained why it removed the internet, and why in-game social media was a better fit for Leonida; "It didn't feel necessary for us," head of development Rob Nelson said. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps.".

Nelson assured that just because GTA 6 doesn't have an in-game internet to browse, that doesn't mean the idea won't return in the future—and Rockstar has hinted that sequels won't take nearly as long to get out the door. But for Leonida, the team wanted players to experience the "meaningful stuff" by focusing on the open world, rather than navigating an interface on their phones. They wanted you to fixate on "doing Grand Theft Auto," engaging with the world's economics and systems instead of mindlessly online shopping for lavish cars.

According to recent reports, "They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of sh*t, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," he continued. "It was never a top-down, 'We're not going to have websites.' I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it.".

Jason and Lucia won't bumble into a sting operation, and you can't order an Oppressor from your phone, but the in-game social media app Snapmatic—Rockstar's answer to Instagram. It has entire feeds with actual pages and posts, so a lot of work has gone into making the online side of GTA 6's world feel as alive and realistic as past entries, just with the focus shifted entirely to social media instead of car dealerships and pyramid schemes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Revision, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

It has been revealed that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Revision to actually see it in action.

In a recent development, the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

In a recent development, the Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside newly introduced Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the substantial day.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nintendo's former marketing leads Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang believe that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake will reinforce how lucrative remakes can be for the company going forward.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is a pretty massive success so far; it instantly became the biggest physical launch of 2026 in the UK so far, as well as the US, and the second best-selling Nintendo Switch 2 game after Mario Kart World (which was bundled with the console), with its 5.2 million sales.

This comes after Star Fox had a pretty good time with its N64 remake released earlier this year, and of course years and years of Sony, Capcom, Konami, and everyone else going to the remake well over the years.

Ellis notes it "does reinforce" Nintendo's direction with these projects, which is "remakes can be really lucrative and really popular.".

While remakes can be effectively used to fill a place in a schedule without the need to go all-in on a newly introduced game – as we saw with Star Fox earlier this year – "if you have the right game and you do it in the right way it can be one of your biggest releases on the platform," which seems very likely to hold in Ocarina of Time's case.

Yang adds, "You're looking at the numbers, and you think, you're saying to yourself like, 'Wow, I didn't put as much effort into something' in comparison to something like Tears of the Kingdom or Breath of the Wild, which had very long development cycles, but still 'I made a lot of money.'".

As for what Nintendo should remake, Yang points out franchises that could be reignited by a remake – like Star Fox seemingly has been – such as Golden Sun. While Ellis puts out there that Super Smash Bros. Melee should be the one. There's been a lot of talk about "what do you do after Ultimate?" and a remake of the series' most beloved game could give the devs "some time to figure it out.".

However, due to the fanatical community Melee has, he doesn't know if it could happen, as "this is the ultimate example of the fan base being ready to revolt on the slightest change.".

Mario and Zelda creator Shigeru Miyamoto to receive once-per-decade Legend Award for "creators whose groundbreaking achievements have already earned lasting universal acclaim".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As covered by our pals over at Time Extension, Mitsuda-san believes that without Akira Toriyama – who sadly passed away in 2024 – the Dragon Quest franchise cannot continue imitating the iconic artist's signature style.

The catalyst for this comment was the release of a new mobile game titled Dragon Quest RPG: The Cursed Tree And the Chosen Isle, which features artwork strikingly similar to Toriyama-san's work.

Here's what the blog post noted:.

Recent findings suggest that “Dragon Quest RPG‘s Toriyama-san-styled illustration has become a hot topic, but for the illustrator, for Akira Toriyama fans, and for the now-deceased Akira Toriyama himself, I don’t feel this is a good direction for everyone involved. In my personal opinion, since it’s no longer possible to create anything upcoming no matter how hard one tries, it might be time to end the Dragon Quest series, and for Yuji Horii to create a new RPG. (There are a lot of remakes out there, after all).”.

Online speculation, highlighted by Power Up Gaming, also points at the potential involvement of generative AI to create the in-game characters. However, despite enthusiasm around the technology from creator Yuji Horii, there's doesn't seem to be any legitimate evidence that this is the case.

Regardless, Mitsuda-san does have a point. Dragon Quest is synonymous with Toriyama-san's art style, and it might be tricky to maintain this without the man himself at the helm. Indeed, reaction to Dragon Quest XII: Beyond Dreams hasn't exactly been universally positive, with some online consumers criticising the design of the main protagonist.

We think it's unlikely that Dragon Quest will end anytime soon, however. The series is still incredibly popular to this day, and continues to sell ludicrous numbers in Japan especially. Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World is scheduled to release on Switch 1 and 2 on 3rd December 2026.

What do you make of Mitsuda-san's comments here regarding Dragon Quest? Should the series end? Or do you think it just needs to adopt a different art style going forward? Let us know.

[source procyon-studio.com, via timeextension.com].

Industry observers note that expensive British department store Selfridges has launched a sizeable Grand Theft Auto 6 takeover, completely making-over its Oxford Street London Corner Shop store and offering a considerable line of clothing, which includes an exclusive varsity jacket that costs a bank-melting £2,500. Note, you can buy the GTA 6 items online as well.

Live from Selfridges at Oxford Street for the #GTAVI activation🌴Rockstar are not messing around 🤯 pic.twitter.com/vqqXKwB1oJ.

That GTA 6 varsity jacket is by far and away the most expensive item (and it's apparently already sold out), next to a non-exclusive varsity jacket that's £1,750, whereas the other items are pricey but conceivably affordable.

There are a few ranges on offer. There's a nice bright teal and pink-coloured range based around the spoof NFL team the Vice City Manatees, which includes a manatee plushie, an American football, a jacket, and other bits and bobs. There's also a range based around the spoof NBA team, the Vice City Narcos, that includes a basketball (there's a standard GTA 6-branded basketball too).

According to recent reports, there's a range based on the spoof fast-food chain Burger Shot, which includes a visor, work uniform, and apron, amusingly. There are some admirably horrid postcard-decorated shirts and shorts, and there's a lot of generic game-branded caps and T-shirts besides, all in quite nice colours. Quirky branded offerings include an ashtray, money clip and dartboard. It's all quite attractive stuff.

There's no word on how long the items will be stocked for or that the Selfridges Corner Shop takeover will run for, other than "while stocks last".

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto 6 arrives 19th November - next week - so the hype machine is now in full effect. GTA 6 pre-load dates, times and details have been announced, and we know what the GTA 6 Trophies and Achievements will be.

Rockstar were "definitely" thinking about giving a Japanese studio the keys to GTA, claims former tech director - "I have a name, but I'm not gonna say it"

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (853 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since time immemorial, North American and European publishers have racked their brains over ways to make their games sell in Japan, ancient heartland of mythical beings like Mario, Sonic, and Polaroid Pete.
  • In a recent development, speaking to me last week, Rockstar North's former technical director Obbe Vermeij shared a little about the abandoned project.
  • Rockstar's parent tech giant Take-Two Interactive filed a trademark for GTA Tokyo back in 2003, the year before the release of the Los Angeles-flavoured GTA: San Andreas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since time immemorial, North American and European publishers have racked their brains over ways to make their games sell in Japan, ancient heartland of mythical beings like Mario, Sonic, and Polaroid Pete. In the late noughties, Microsoft rolled out a big push to give Japanese youth the Xbox virus with such targeted console exclusives as Blue Dragon and Lost Odyssey. And Rockstar once dreamed of making a Grand Theft Auto game set in Tokyo.

In a recent development, speaking to me last week, Rockstar North's former technical director Obbe Vermeij shared a little about the abandoned project. Emphasis on the "little" – it doesn't appear to have gotten very far, despite recently unearthed allusions to "Tokyo PS2" in GTA 5's source code.

Rockstar's parent tech giant Take-Two Interactive filed a trademark for GTA Tokyo back in 2003, the year before the release of the Los Angeles-flavoured GTA: San Andreas. At the time, Rockstar were apparently looking at collaborating with a Japanese studio on the project. "So this was kind above my pay grade," Vermeij told me. "But yeah, there were negotiations with studios, and I have a name, but I'm not gonna say it, because then it becomes like a bigger thing than it is, and I'll probably get it wrong, and I don't know how far the negotiations were, how serious it was. I mean, it was definitely serious. It was the blueprint. But I don't know how close it got to actually happening.".

In a recent development, the game itself would likely have been a contemporary story, not a historical yarn like Rockstar's subsequent Red Dead Redemption. "It definitely had samurai swords in it, I remember that, but I think it was present-day probably," Vermeij went on. "Or sort of not too [far off] - it wasn't, like, sort of the medieval era in Japanese history, or anything. It was definitely not like that.".

Recent findings suggest that vermeij was at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009, where he worked on the first four mainline 3D GTA games, plus some handheld spin-offs. During that time, he says, Rockstar frequently considered the idea of a Grand Theft Auto set outside the United States. "In the same way that we were always thinking about other games, we also thought about cities that would be cool, and it was always the same list," he remarked. "It was Moscow, London. Istanbul, Rio de Janeiro, maybe Paris and Tokyo. It was always the same ones that people suggested.".

Grand Theft Auto has never quite the money-spinner in Japan that it is in North America and Europe. Localised editions of the original three 3D GTA games were published by Capcom, sometime after the original releases, selling a few hundred thousand copies apiece in their launch years.

In a recent development, "I think perhaps [Rockstar's co-founders] the Housers were a little annoyed that GTA wasn't as substantial in Japan as they thought it deserved to be," Vermeij reflected. "So it kind of made sense to get a local studio to do it. Japanese people actually kind of like different games from westerners a fair bit. For instance, they don't like first person shooters and stuff. So, it made sense to have a Japanese studio have a shot at it, and I think it would have been really cool, because you know, a GTA made by somebody else in Japanese culture – that's something I would probably play.".

Recent findings suggest that take-Two ultimately abandoned their original "GTA Tokyo" trademark in 2008. It's not clear how much Rockstar have considered setting GTA overseas since Vermeij's day, but co-founder Dan Houser (who left the manufacturer in 2020) recently told podcaster Lex Fridman that they ultimately decided it wasn't a credible objective.

“We made a little thing in London 26 years ago - GTA London - for the top-down for PS1," he noted. "That was pretty cute and fun, as the first mission pack ever for PlayStation 1. I think for a full GTA game, we always decided there was so much Americana inherent in the IP, it would be really hard to make it work in London or anywhere else. You know, you needed guns, you needed these larger-than-life characters. It just felt like the game was so much about America, possibly from an outsider's perspective. But that was so much about what the thing was that it wouldn't really have worked in the same way elsewhere.”.

If this article has left you pining for the Shibuya Scramble NPC-tipping sim that will never be, I bring good news: Japanese developers are quite capable of making their own urban open worlders. The obvious go-tos are Sega's Yakuza/Like A Dragon games, with their abundance of lovingly modelled eateries and discount stores. There's also Ghostwire: Tokyo, a respectable first-person parkour sim, though this particular incarnation of Tokyo has a lot of paranormal congestion. All these games have the advantage of being playable on PC right now. As for GTA 6? Who can say, but Vermeij thinks Rockstar might want to port it sooner to get ahead of the slopcomp craze.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

Industry observers note that as his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:.

It has been revealed that cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Sources indicate that cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” notes game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

In addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override releases in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What do you mean bad actors I wasn’t doing that much bad things pic.twitter.com/swHfeOLTuVNovember 16, 2026.

According to recent reports, bitly, the URL shortener website, got in hot water this week as people (or 'bad actors' as the tech giant calls them) found out they could hijack old broken links and put whatever they like in their place. As you can imagine, chaos ensued.

In a recent development, many of the links have since been fixed, but it seems like the McDonald's Twitter account once accidentally remarked the Swedish McDonald's team are responsible for 9/11,, and KFC linked to the Mewgenics wiki page for Steven, an NPC from the game. McDonald's was caught multiple times in this hijacking, with the Canadian X account hijacked to link the We Are Charlie Kirk song.

Though it's hard to verify now, it also seems like the Windows X page accidentally linked to the "r/FuckMicrosoft" subreddit too.

Major brands weren't the only ones caught in the mass hijacking. President Donald Trump seemingly tweeted a lot of Bitly links back in 2011, which were hijacked to instead link to a 'Trollface' meme song, a picture of a soggy cat titled "Soggy cat", and a link to the Epstein files Wikipedia page.

images for archival purposes pic.twitter.com/fRRr8LMGeENovember 15, 2026.

In a recent development, A day after this exploit started to make its way around X, Bitly shared that it had identified the concern and mentioned, "We have suspended the accounts involved and are disabling the affected links. Our Trust and Safety team is working to address the issue and strengthen protections against similar misuse in the future.".

In a recent development, it seems like the links in question were broken before being hijacked, and customers simply managed to redirect those links to whatever site they wanted. However, in Bitly's documentation, it notes the "back-halves used on these links cannot be re-used — whether they're automatically-generated or custom back-halves." So it's not entirely clear how these users manage to use links when Bitly says they supposedly cannot be reused.

In a recent development, earlier today, we identified an issue that allowed bad actors to repurpose certain old, inactive links to redirect people to content unrelated to the original posts. We have suspended the accounts involved and are disabling the affected links. Our Trust and Safety team is working…November 15, 2026.

In the grand scheme, brands linking to various songs and Wikipedia articles are relatively harmless, but the ability to hijack links does pose a problem: what if hackers could do the same with a link to something containing malware? As such, it's probably a good reminder to Bitly and any other URL shortener websites to double-check that owners can't reuse old broken links, as who knows who could have possibly made them first.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially rolled out.
  • The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.
  • Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially rolled out. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually demonstrated up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Recent findings suggest that numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xenoblade series developer Monolith Soft and Bandai Namco Studios have been listed as support studios for the Switch 2 version of Ocarina of Time, working on elements of the title such as "art, including characters, terrain, animations, cutscenes and UI". Special thanks to both companies appear in the credits for the newly-debuted game (as you can see below) and a statement released by Bandai Namco Studios confirms its involvement, too.

In a recent development, "We were commissioned to produce some of the visual assets and artwork, including characters, environments, animations, cutscenes, and UI elements, for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, a Nintendo Switch 2 game released by Nintendo Co., Ltd. on 5th November, 2026," reads a translated release from Bandai Namco Studio reads.

According to recent reports, of course, this isn't the first time we've seen Bandai Namco Studios' talents leveraged to help with Nintendo games: the publisher and its internal studios worked closely with Nintendo as a co-developer on the long-awaited Metroid Prime 4, and we know the studios are listed as co-developer for first-party Switch 2 titles like Mario Kart World and Splatoon Raiders. Typically, the work carried out by Bandai Namco comes from one of two dedicated internal studios that are contracted specifically to work with Nintendo: Studio 2 and Studio S. You can see a full list of the games Bandai Namco's support studios have worked on here. You'll note there are many Nintendo first-party titles listed here, going back to 2012 and Mario Kart 8. In late 2025, Nintendo acquired Bandai Namco Studios Singapore from the publisher, renaming the tech giant Nintendo Studios Singapore.

Industry observers note that "Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve," wrote our reviewer, Christian Donlan, in his five-star review of the Switch 2 game last week. "This is Ocarina as it's always been, as timeless and intricate, but it also has a vibrancy and clarity that makes it feel like it was just created last Wednesday.".

If - somehow! - you've already gobbled up most of the game and you're keen to play it again, you will be pleased to know that Master Quest code has been found in datamined files for the title, suggesting DLC may well be on the way in the not-too-distant future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ostensible graphics card tech giant and definite AI giants Nvidia have commissioned an independent investigation into themselves, amid reports that CEO Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

It has been revealed that per both the New York Times and Nvidia themselves, Nvidia offered to go under the microscope after US intelligence organisations elected to investigate Huang’s paramour, Chinese national Alice Huang (no, uh, relation, and also known as Huang Le), on suspicion of sharing sensitive information with Beijing. The Nvidia-running, leather-jacketed Huang has thus far only copped to an unspecified affair, admitting in an extraordinary public statement that he was "unfaithful to my wife." Still, the two investigations are likely to start a bizarre new leg in the alread-messy AI arms race that the US and China have been indulging in for years.

See, the basis for Huang and Huang’s relationship appears to be the same thing that’s been fucking us as PC owners: data centres and AI hardware. Alice Huang is a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre firm who’ve bought billions of US dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips – and have been investigated for allegedly getting some of them into the hands of Chinese companies, in defiance of US trade restrictions on goods that might threaten the States’ AI dominance. Possibly also, given both countries’ increasing interest in the technology’s military uses, their perception of national security.

Many of these embargo-dodging accusations originate from after Alice Huang left Megaspeed, though she is now under that separate investigation for intelligence-sharing, and the prospect of any high-tech pillow talk from the lips of someone like Jensen Huang would be very disturbing to the feds indeed. Both Nvidia and their "deeply sorry" CEO deny that he shared sensitive information beyond that required for routine customer/client discussions.

"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the firm’s statement reads. "Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.".

In the US-Sino battle of artificial intelligence, Jensen Huang has – as with his marriage – played both sides. He’s undoubtedly been a, perhaps the driving force behind reinventing Nvidia from beloved makers of gaming gear to the US’ number-one purveyors of environment-ruining, brain-polluting slop technology. But after the Biden administration banned American-made GPU exports to China over fears they’d be used to boost the latter’s military capabilities, Huang successfully lobbied Donald Trump into relaxing those restrictions, allowing Nvidia to flog their wares – including their crème de la crème AI GPU, the H200 – to cash-rich Chinese companies.

Industry observers note that in a further twist, many of those chips have got mysteriously stuck in Hong Kong import facilities, suggesting the Chinese government in fact wants AI companies to stick to Chinese-made parts. But then, the Hangzhou-based DeepSeek reportedly trained their latest AI model on illicitly-gained Nvidia tech, so there’s either a healthy black market in operation, or the CCP is willing to tolerate the occasional bit of decadent Western silicone if it helps them catch up to the burger-chomping likes of ChatGPT and Claude. Maybe both, and either way, one can see how a well-placed honeypot could prove useful. Allegedly.

Without wanting to pick sides, in a race where I hope both teams lose, it’s also China who have more work to do. The People’s Republic produces a greater proportion of successful 'open' AI models, where the inner workings and even source code is made public, and mines more of the crucial minerals needed to build components and infrastructure. However, US-produced 'closed' models dominate global AI usage, and despite the lack of minerals, its existing data centres are estimated to wield 40 times the combined compute power of China’s. Probably because they just get all the RAM they need from Best Buy instead of digging it up themselves.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love.
  • It has been revealed that as is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year.
  • Sources indicate that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

It has been revealed that as is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

Sources indicate that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be unveiled tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

Industry observers note that this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Industry observers note that last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what upcoming horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

According to recent reports, look, I'll be real with you. When I installed Drag Meets – Quick n Dirty Edition, I was not expecting it to go well. Cars spend most of their time flying and exploding in my copy of Grand Theft Auto 5, and these circumstances aren't conducive to gentlemanly racing.

I didn't anticipate it going quite as badly as it did, though. Drag Meets is actually rather complex: you don't just rock up to an objective marker, tap E, and get warped behind the wheel of a car. There's a lite social sim element to the whole thing, so you walk up to an objective marker, tap E, and suddenly find yourself standing in the midst of a drag racing soirée.

Drag meets are a scene, it turns out, and the scene's members have names, goals, and ambitions. A racer named "Blue Anime Panto" is seeking a challenger, the notifications inform me. "Blade had joined the meet", reads another. A lady called Tempesta has been forced to leave the meet because her engine broke, apparently. How did this happen? Either it's a randomly rolled event or her car flew into the sun; I am unable to tell.

It's not just Tempesta who's leaving the meet. Everyone is leaving, on account of the airborne minivan, just overhead, filled with hitmen determined to kill us all. They should be determined to kill me and only me, but Lamar (from GTA 5, you know? Lamar was also there. Keep up) began shooting back at them and all hell broke loose.

Industry observers note that the drag race—if it's even possible—never got the opportunity to start. Pretty soon, racing legends like Stinger GT and Rhapsody were face-down in the Los Santos grass. And then I teleported to the airport.
